<script>
function saveSvgFromParentDiv(divElId, name) {
  var divSvgWrapperEl = document.getElementById(divElId);

  var svgEl = divSvgWrapperEl.firstElementChild;
  svgEl.setAttribute("xmlns", "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg");
  var svgData = svgEl.outerHTML;
  var preface = '<?xml version="1.0" standalone="no"?>\r\n';
  var svgBlob = new Blob([preface, svgData], {type:"image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8"});
  var svgUrl = URL.createObjectURL(svgBlob);
  var downloadLink = document.createElement("a");
  downloadLink.href = svgUrl;
  downloadLink.download = name;
  document.body.appendChild(downloadLink);
  downloadLink.click();
  document.body.removeChild(downloadLink);
}

function saveSvgFromParentDiv2(clickedEl, downloadName) {

  var svgEl = clickedEl.previousElementSibling;
  svgEl.setAttribute("xmlns", "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg");
  var svgData = svgEl.outerHTML;
  var preface = '<?xml version="1.0" standalone="no"?>\r\n';
  var svgBlob = new Blob([preface, svgData], {type:"image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8"});
  var svgUrl = URL.createObjectURL(svgBlob);
  
  _createThenClickImageLink(svgUrl, downloadName);
}

function savePngFromParentDiv(clickedEl, downloadName) {
  var imgEl = clickedEl.previousElementSibling;
  
  _createThenClickImageLink(imgEl.src, downloadName);
}

function _createThenClickImageLink(imageUrl, downloadName) {
  var downloadLink = document.createElement("a");
  downloadLink.href = imageUrl;
  downloadLink.download = downloadName;
  
  document.body.appendChild(downloadLink);
  downloadLink.click(); // triggers image download
  document.body.removeChild(downloadLink);
}
</script>

```{r helpers_png_svg, include=FALSE}

## Creating helper functions for PNG or SVG files ##

#Creating a temp file to load images, to be deleted at the end
if(dir.exists("temp") == FALSE){
  dir.create("temp")
}

# Function createPngOrSvg for creating images from plots
createPngOrSvg <- function(plot_data, image_name, w, h) {
  
  if (format_svg) {
    
    # Code for creating svg images (no temp file)
    s <- svgstring(width=w,height=h)
    plot(plot_data)
    invisible(dev.off())
  
    return(paste0("<div id='svgWrapper'>",s(),"<a class='no-print' href='javascript:void(0);' onclick=\"javascript:saveSvgFromParentDiv2(this,'",image_name,".svg');\" >Save figure</a></div>"))
    
  } else {
    
    # Code for saving png images (temp file used)
    png_file <- paste0("./temp/",image_name, ".png")
    png(filename = png_file, width = w, height = h, type = "cairo")
    plot(plot_data)
    invisible(dev.off())
    
    png_binary <- readBin(png_file, what = "raw", n = file.info(png_file)$size)
    png_base64 <- base64encode(png_binary)
    
     return(paste0("<div id='pngWrapper'> <img src='data:image/png;base64,",png_base64,"' ><a  href='javascript:void(0);' onclick=\"javascript:savePngFromParentDiv(this, '",image_name,".png');\" >Save figure</a></div>"))
    
  }
}

# Function createPngOrSvgForGrid for creating images from grids (heatmaps, for example)
createPngOrSvgForGrid <- function(plot_data1, plot_data2, image_name) {
  
  if (format_svg) {
    
    # Code for creating svg image (no temp file)
    s <- svgstring(width=20,height=10)
    grid.arrange(arrangeGrob(plot_data1), arrangeGrob(plot_data2), ncol=2,nrow=1)
    invisible(dev.off())
  
    return(paste0("<div id='svgWrapper'>",s(),"<a class='no-print' href='javascript:void(0);' onclick=\"javascript:saveSvgFromParentDiv2(this,'",image_name,".svg');\" >Save figure</a></div>"))
    
  } else {
    
    # Code for creating png image (temp file used)
    png_file <- paste0("./temp/",image_name, ".png")
    png(filename = png_file, width = 1200, height = 600, type = "cairo")
    grid.arrange(arrangeGrob(plot_data1), arrangeGrob(plot_data2), ncol=2,nrow=1)
    invisible(dev.off())
    
    png_binary <- readBin(png_file, what = "raw", n = file.info(png_file)$size)
    png_base64 <- base64encode(png_binary)
    
     return(paste0("<div id=pngWrapper><img src='data:image/png;base64,",png_base64,"' ><a  href='javascript:void(0);' onclick=\"javascript:savePngFromParentDiv(this, '",image_name,".png');\" >Save figure</a></div>"))
    
  }
}
```

```{r file_import, echo=FALSE}
## Importing and parsing data file ##

data<- read.csv(params$quant_df, check.names = F, sep="\t")

# Importing experimental design and parameters
expDesign <- read.csv(params$design_exp, header = T, sep="\t")
parameters <- read.csv(params$parameters, header=T, sep="=")

```


```{r param_parsing}

## Parsing parameters ##

# T or F using imputation
imputation <- !as.logical(parameters["No.imputed.values",])

# SVG or PNG images
if(as.character(parameters["Figure.format",]) == "SVG"){
  format_svg <- TRUE
}else{
  format_svg <- FALSE
}

# T or F coloring by group
coloring_by_group <- as.logical(parameters["Color.by.group",])

# Style of volcano plot
Vol_colors <- as.character(parameters["Volcano.color.style",])

# Specified proteins for normalization
Normalization_list <- as.numeric(strsplit(as.character(parameters["Proteins.for.normalization",]),";")[[1]])

# Specified proteins for labeling on volcano plot
Vol_labels <- strsplit(as.character(parameters["Volcano.manual.accession",]),";")[[1]]

# T or F labeling on volcano plot
Vol_no_lab <- as.logical(parameters["Volcano.no.labeling",])

# T or F for normalization
normalization <- as.logical(parameters["Normalization",])

# Notes about deprecated or ignored parameters, printed below the parameters table (and on the console)
parameter_notes <- c()
add_parameter_note <- function(note){
  parameter_notes <<- c(parameter_notes, note)
  cat("Note: ", note, "\n", sep = "", file = stderr())
}

# Returns the value of a parameter (as a character string, NA if absent), accepting a deprecated name
get_parameter <- function(name, deprecated = NULL){
  if (name %in% rownames(parameters)) return(trimws(as.character(parameters[name,])))
  for (old_name in deprecated) {
    if (old_name %in% rownames(parameters)) {
      add_parameter_note(paste0("Parameter ", old_name, " is deprecated, please rename it ", name, "."))
      return(trimws(as.character(parameters[old_name,])))
    }
  }
  NA
}

## Classes of missing values, per protein and condition (k observed values): with Imputation.MCAR.model=knn, MCAR if k >= Imputation.MCAR.min.obs
## and the MS/MS and intensity criteria are met (imputed from the neighbours); otherwise MNAR if k <= Imputation.MNAR.max.obs (imputed with the
## background noise); left missing otherwise.

# MCAR imputation: "none" (no MCAR imputation) or "knn" (MCAR values imputed from the neighbours). "MNAR" is the former name of "none".
imputation_method <- trimws(as.character(parameters["Imputation.MCAR.model",]))
if (!is.na(imputation_method) && imputation_method == "MNAR") {
  add_parameter_note("Imputation.MCAR.model=MNAR is deprecated, please use Imputation.MCAR.model=none (same behaviour: the missing values are imputed with the background noise, within the limit of Imputation.MNAR.max.obs).")
  imputation_method <- "none"
}
if (is.na(imputation_method) || !imputation_method %in% c("none", "knn")) {
  stop("Parameter Imputation.MCAR.model must be none or knn.")
}

# Maximum number of observed values in a condition for the missing values to be MNAR (no limit if absent: all the missing values
# that are not MCAR are imputed with the background noise)
Imputation.MNAR.max.obs = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(get_parameter("Imputation.MNAR.max.obs")))
if (!"Imputation.MNAR.max.obs" %in% rownames(parameters) || trimws(as.character(parameters["Imputation.MNAR.max.obs",])) == "") {
  Imputation.MNAR.max.obs = Inf
} else if (is.na(Imputation.MNAR.max.obs) || Imputation.MNAR.max.obs < 0) {
  stop("Parameter Imputation.MNAR.max.obs must be a number greater than or equal to 0 (or be removed for no limit).")
}

# Setting minimum knn occurances
Imputation.knn.min.occurrences = as.numeric(as.character(parameters["Imputation.knn.min.occurrences",]))

# Minimum number of observed values and of MS/MS identifications in a condition for the missing values to be MCAR
Imputation.MCAR.min.obs = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(get_parameter("Imputation.MCAR.min.obs", deprecated = "Imputation.MCAR.threshold.obs")))
Imputation.MCAR.min.MSMS = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(get_parameter("Imputation.MCAR.min.MSMS", deprecated = "Imputation.MCAR.threshold.MSMS")))

# Intensity criterion of the MCAR classification: "auto" (cutoff estimated from the missing-value rate against the intensity), "Q1" or "none"
Imputation.MCAR.intensity.cutoff = if ("Imputation.MCAR.intensity.cutoff" %in% rownames(parameters)) trimws(as.character(parameters["Imputation.MCAR.intensity.cutoff",])) else "auto"

if (imputation_method == "knn") {
  if (is.na(Imputation.MCAR.min.obs) || Imputation.MCAR.min.obs < 2) {
    stop("Parameter Imputation.MCAR.min.obs must be at least 2 (the variability of a protein needs at least 2 observed values).")
  }
  if (is.finite(Imputation.MNAR.max.obs) && Imputation.MNAR.max.obs >= Imputation.MCAR.min.obs) {
    stop("Parameter Imputation.MNAR.max.obs must be lower than Imputation.MCAR.min.obs.")
  }
  if (is.na(Imputation.MCAR.min.MSMS) || Imputation.MCAR.min.MSMS < 0) {
    stop("Parameter Imputation.MCAR.min.MSMS must be a number greater than or equal to 0.")
  }
  if (is.na(Imputation.knn.min.occurrences) || Imputation.knn.min.occurrences < 2) {
    stop("Parameter Imputation.knn.min.occurrences must be at least 2.")
  }
  if (!Imputation.MCAR.intensity.cutoff %in% c("auto", "Q1", "none")) {
    stop("Parameter Imputation.MCAR.intensity.cutoff must be auto, Q1 or none.")
  }
}

# Getting MNAR model
Imputation.MNAR.model <- parameters["Imputation.MNAR.model",]

# Setting MNAR model percentile cutoff
Imputation.MNAR.percentage <- as.numeric(as.character(parameters["Imputation.MNAR.percentile",]))

# Removed parameters: the fold change is always the ratio of the mean intensities (fc)
if ("Fold.Change" %in% rownames(parameters)) {
  if (trimws(as.character(parameters["Fold.Change",])) != "fc") {
    stop("Parameter Fold.Change=", parameters["Fold.Change",], " is no longer supported: the fold change is always the ratio of the mean intensities. Please remove the Fold.Change parameter.")
  }
  add_parameter_note("Parameter Fold.Change is no longer used (the fold change is always fc) and can be removed.")
}
if ("Test.adjust.FDR" %in% rownames(parameters)) {
  add_parameter_note("Parameter Test.adjust.FDR is no longer used and can be removed: with a multiple testing correction, Stat.threshold.significance is the FDR threshold applied to the adjusted p-values.")
}

# Significance threshold: applied to the adjusted p-values (q-values) if a multiple testing correction is selected, to the raw p-values otherwise
Stat.threshold.significance = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(get_parameter("Stat.threshold.significance", deprecated = "Volcano.threshold.pvalue")))
if (is.na(Stat.threshold.significance) || Stat.threshold.significance <= 0 || Stat.threshold.significance > 1) {
  stop("Parameter Stat.threshold.significance must be a number greater than 0 and at most 1 (e.g. 0.05).")
}

# Fold change threshold, expressed as an absolute log2 fold change (e.g. 0.58 for a 1.5-fold change)
Stat.threshold.fc = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(get_parameter("Stat.threshold.fc", deprecated = "Volcano.threshold.fc")))
if (is.na(Stat.threshold.fc) || Stat.threshold.fc < 0) {
  stop("Parameter Stat.threshold.fc must be a single number greater than or equal to 0 (an absolute log2 fold change, e.g. 0.58 for a 1.5-fold change).")
}

# Setting pvalue calculation test type
Test.type <- parameters["Test.type",]

# If using logged values for significance test (T/F)
Test.log <- parameters["Test.log",]

# Setting conditions for DA comparison
comparisons_to_display = strsplit(as.character(parameters["Comparisons",]),";")[[1]]

# Setting if test is paired
Test.paired <- as.logical(parameters["Test.paired",])

# Post-hoc procedure of the anova / kruskall tests, for the pairwise comparisons: "holm" (default) or "bonferroni" (pairwise tests
# corrected over the comparisons of each protein), or "tukey" (anova only)
Test.posthoc.procedure <- if ("Test.posthoc.procedure" %in% rownames(parameters)) trimws(as.character(parameters["Test.posthoc.procedure",])) else "holm"

# Gating of the anova / kruskall comparisons by the global test: "none" (default) or "bh" (comparisons tested only for the proteins whose
# global test passes Stat.threshold.significance after a BH correction across proteins)
Test.anova.gating <- if ("Test.anova.gating" %in% rownames(parameters)) trimws(as.character(parameters["Test.anova.gating",])) else "none"
if (Test.type %in% c("anova", "kruskall")) {
  if (!Test.posthoc.procedure %in% c("holm", "bonferroni", "tukey", "none")) stop("Parameter Test.posthoc.procedure must be holm, bonferroni, tukey or none.")
  if (Test.type == "kruskall" && Test.posthoc.procedure == "tukey") stop("Test.posthoc.procedure=tukey requires Test.type=anova (use holm, bonferroni or none with kruskall).")
  if (!Test.anova.gating %in% c("none", "bh")) stop("Parameter Test.anova.gating must be none or bh.")
}

# The p-value of the global test over all the conditions (anova or Kruskal-Wallis) and its q-value are exported with
# Test.type=anova or kruskall and more than one comparison
export_global_test <- Test.type %in% c("anova", "kruskall") && length(comparisons_to_display) > 1

# Pairing of the samples in a paired test: "position" (order in the experimental design, default) or "name" (same repBio)
Test.paired.by <- if ("Test.paired.by" %in% rownames(parameters)) trimws(as.character(parameters["Test.paired.by",])) else "position"
if (Test.paired && !Test.paired.by %in% c("position", "name")) {
  stop("Parameter Test.paired.by must be position or name.")
}

# Setting for equal variance
Test.var.equal <- as.logical(parameters["Test.var.equal",])

# Setting alternative options for testing
alternative=as.character(parameters["Test.alternative",])

# Setting test adjustment procedure
Test.adjust.procedure <- as.character(parameters["Test.adjust.procedure",])


```

```{r validate_inputs}

## Checking that the experimental design, the quantification table and the comparisons are consistent ##
## (per-sample columns are then selected by their exact names, see group_cols()) ##

validate_inputs(data, expDesign, comparisons = comparisons_to_display, required_columns = c("Accession", "Gene_name", "Specific_peptides"))

# Saving original accession columns before pre-processing
# (for later joining to original in output_file)
og_Acc <- data[grepl("Accession",colnames(data))]

# Creating a display label for each for each protein
# Using Gene_name when available, Accession otherwise
# Making sure Labels are unique
data <- data %>% mutate(Label=Gene_name) %>%
  relocate(Label,.after = "Gene_name") %>%
  mutate(Label=if_else(is.na(Label),Accession,Label)) %>% #if gene_name is NA, use Accession
  group_by(Label) %>%
   mutate(Label = case_when(
    n() > 1 ~ paste0(Label, "_", Accession),  # Modify only duplicated labels
    TRUE ~ Label  # Keep unique labels as they are
  )) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r group_definition, results='asis'}

## Parsing to group samples based on the experimental design input file ##

group_ids <- unique(expDesign$Condition)

# Sample ids ("<repBio>_<Condition>") of each group, used as prefix of all the per-sample columns
# (stored in a named list rather than assign(), so that a condition name cannot overwrite another variable)
group_samples <- lapply(setNames(as.list(group_ids), group_ids), function(group){
  paste0(unique(expDesign$repBio[which(expDesign$Condition==group)]),"_",group)
})

# Returns the exact names of the per-sample columns of the given groups, "<sample id><suffix>", in experimental design order.
# If 'available' is given (column names of the table to subset), stops when an expected column is missing.
group_cols <- function(groups, suffix, available = NULL){
  cols <- paste0(unlist(group_samples[as.character(groups)], use.names = FALSE), suffix)
  if (!is.null(available)) {
    missing_cols <- setdiff(cols, available)
    if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
      stop("Missing column(s) for group(s) ", paste(groups, collapse = ", "), ": ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
    }
  }
  cols
}

# Paired tests: returns, for the columns of condition B (in group_cols order), the order that puts each replicate of B in front of
# its pair in condition A (columns of A in group_cols order). With Test.paired.by=position, the i-th replicate of A (in the order of
# the experimental design) is paired with the i-th replicate of B; with Test.paired.by=name, replicates with the same repBio are paired.
paired_order <- function(A_name, B_name){
  reps_A <- unique(as.character(expDesign$repBio[expDesign$Condition == A_name]))
  reps_B <- unique(as.character(expDesign$repBio[expDesign$Condition == B_name]))
  if (Test.paired.by == "position") {
    if (length(reps_A) != length(reps_B)) {
      stop("Paired test: conditions ", A_name, " and ", B_name, " must have the same number of replicates (", length(reps_A), " and ", length(reps_B), ").")
    }
    return(seq_along(reps_B))
  }
  if (length(reps_A) != length(reps_B) || !setequal(reps_A, reps_B)) {
    stop("Paired test: conditions ", A_name, " and ", B_name, " must have the same replicate names (repBio column of the experimental design) with Test.paired.by=name. ",
         A_name, ": ", paste(reps_A, collapse = ", "), "; ", B_name, ": ", paste(reps_B, collapse = ", "), ". Use Test.paired.by=position to pair them by their order.")
  }
  match(reps_A, reps_B)
}

# Paired tests: text listing the pairs of replicates used for a comparison
paired_text <- function(A_name, B_name){
  reps_A <- unique(as.character(expDesign$repBio[expDesign$Condition == A_name]))
  reps_B <- unique(as.character(expDesign$repBio[expDesign$Condition == B_name]))[paired_order(A_name, B_name)]
  paste0("Pairs (", A_name, " - ", B_name, ", by ", Test.paired.by, "): ", paste0(reps_A, " - ", reps_B, collapse = ", "), ".")
}

# Returns a lookup table giving the group of each per-sample column "<sample id><suffix>"
group_of_cols <- function(suffix){
  setNames(rep(names(group_samples), lengths(group_samples)), paste0(unlist(group_samples, use.names = FALSE), suffix))
}
```

```{r coloring_by_group}

## Parses sample group names from raw data file ##

if(coloring_by_group){
  
  # Parsing group names from experimental design
  sample_names = expDesign$Condition
  
  l <- length(group_ids)

  # brewer.pal() is limited to 8 colors for Set2 (and needs n >= 3)
  if(l <= 8){
    group_colors <- brewer.pal(8, "Set2")[seq_len(l)]
  }else{
    group_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))(l)
  }

  # Matching sample colors to samples in the same group, named by sample
  # so that scale_color_manual() maps them by name rather than by position
  color_map <- setNames(group_colors, group_ids)
  sample_colors <- color_map[sample_names]
  names(sample_colors) <- sub("Intensity_", "", expDesign$File)
  
}

```

```{r mean_technical_replicates_function}

## Combining technical replicates into biological-replicate-level means ##

# Returns the bio-rep level tables computed from the intensity columns "<File><suffix>" of the quantification table:
# [[1]] abundance ("<repBio>_<Condition>_mean" columns), [[2]] identification type ("<repBio>_<Condition>_identification_type" columns)
average_technical_replicates <- function(data, suffix){

  # Creating data frame containing ID - from data - for mean_abundance
  mean_abundance_repbio = data.frame(data$Id)
  colnames(mean_abundance_repbio) = "Id"

  # Creating data frame containing ID - from data - for mean_identification_type
  mean_identification_type_repbio = data.frame(data$Id)
  colnames(mean_identification_type_repbio) = "Id"

  # Looping over each experimental condition or "group"
  for(group in group_ids){

    # Taking the subset of experimental design associated with this condition
    sub = subset(expDesign,expDesign$Condition==group)

    # Looping over each replicate within this condition
    for (rBio in unique(sub$repBio)){

      # Getting intensity columns and converting their names to the corresponding identification type column names
      samples_intensities = subset(sub,sub$repBio==rBio)$File
      samples_identification_type = paste0("Identification_type",sub("Intensity","",samples_intensities))

      # if a bio-rep contains multiple technical replicates
      if(length(samples_intensities)>1){

        # Average the abundance/intensity values, and appending then to the end of bio-rep table
        mean_ab = rowMeans(data[paste0(as.character(samples_intensities),suffix)],na.rm=T)
        mean_abundance_repbio = cbind(mean_abundance_repbio,mean_ab)

        # Collapsing identification types across technical replicates, if not classified as "By MS/MS" classify as "By matching".
        id_type = apply(data[samples_identification_type],1,function(x) ifelse("By MS/MS"%in%x,"By MS/MS","By matching"))
        mean_identification_type_repbio = cbind(mean_identification_type_repbio,id_type)

      }else{ # If a bio-rep has only one technical replicate

        # Copying original abundance/intensity column
        mean_abundance_repbio = cbind(mean_abundance_repbio,data[paste0(as.character(samples_intensities),suffix)])
        mean_identification_type_repbio = cbind(mean_identification_type_repbio,data[samples_identification_type])

      }

      # Renaming most recent mean abundance column to include "_mean" and identification column to include "_identification_type"
      colnames(mean_abundance_repbio)[ncol(mean_abundance_repbio)] = paste0(rBio,"_",group,"_mean")
      colnames(mean_identification_type_repbio)[ncol(mean_identification_type_repbio)] = paste0(rBio,"_",group,"_identification_type")
    }
  }

  return(list(mean_abundance_repbio, mean_identification_type_repbio))
}
```


```{r proteins_filtered_diagramm}

## Parsing of data input file to separate by specific peptides ##

# Creating function for dataset filtering
filter_dataset <- function(data, group_ids){
  
  # Remove proteins with 0 specific peptides (Specific_peptides is a required column, see validate_inputs)
  nb = nrow(data)
  data = subset(data,data[,"Specific_peptides"]>0)
  nb_specific = nb-nrow(data)
   
  ## Creates a filtered data set based in the raw data file given in the parameters. Flags and filters out any specific protein that has insufficient data. If the final filtered data set is empty, throws an error ##
  
  # Parsing minimum required thresholds from parameters
  Filter.threshold.obs = as.numeric(as.character(parameters["Filter.threshold.obs",]))
  Filter.threshold.ms = as.numeric(as.character(parameters["Filter.threshold.ms",]))
  
  # MS/MS filter: counting all "By MS/MS" per protein across the identification type columns
  id_cols = grep("Identification_type_", colnames(data))
  msms_counts = rowSums(data[, id_cols, drop = FALSE] == "By MS/MS", na.rm = TRUE)

  # If number of MS/MS identifications is below threshold, exclude the protein
  fail_ms = msms_counts < Filter.threshold.ms

  # Observation filter: for each group, compute the fraction of observed bio-replicate mean values.
  # A protein is found insufficient only if the fraction is below the threshold in ALL groups
  fail_obs_all_groups = rep(TRUE, nrow(data))
  for (group in group_ids) {
    mean_cols = group_cols(group, "_mean", colnames(data))
    group_vals = data[, mean_cols, drop = FALSE]
    nonNA_frac = rowSums(!is.na(group_vals)) / ncol(group_vals)
    fail_obs_all_groups = fail_obs_all_groups & (nonNA_frac < Filter.threshold.obs)
  }

  # A protein is excluded for # observations only if it passed the MS/MS filter
  fail_obs = !fail_ms & fail_obs_all_groups

  # Keep proteins that pass both filters, and count the excluded ones
  filtered_data = data[!fail_ms & !fail_obs_all_groups, ]
  nb_ms = sum(fail_ms)
  nb_obs = sum(fail_obs)

  # Count the number of proteins in the filtered dataset
  nbProteins = nrow(filtered_data)

  # Subset of mean_abundance for filtered proteins
  mean_abundance_repbio = filtered_data[,grepl("_mean|Id$",names(filtered_data))]
  
  # If the sub-dataset for mean_abundance is 0 (all proteins filtered out), throw error
  if (nrow(mean_abundance_repbio) == 0) {
    stop("Can't continue since the number of rows after applied filters is zero. Please check 'Filter.threshold' parameters (try to set lower values).")
  }
  
  ## Designing and framing of 'Proteins Filtered' bar chart ##
  
  # Summary table for filtering results
  diagrammDFT <- data.frame(
    filter = c("No specific peptides",
              paste0("Less than ",(Filter.threshold.obs * 100),"% observations in at least one group"), 
              paste0("Less than ",Filter.threshold.ms," files identified by MS/MS"),
              "Proteins kept for analysis"),
    value = c(nb_specific, nb_obs, nb_ms, nbProteins)
    ) %>%
    mutate(value.percent = round(.$value / sum(.$value) * 100, 1),
           filter = factor(.$filter, levels = .$filter[1:4]))
  
  # Diagram to be used for the bar plot
  diagrammDF <- data.frame(
    filter = c(paste0(diagrammDFT$value[1], " (", diagrammDFT$value.percent[1], "%) No specific peptides"),
              paste0(diagrammDFT$value[2], " (", diagrammDFT$value.percent[2],"%) Less than ",(Filter.threshold.obs * 100),"% observations in at least one group"), 
              paste0(diagrammDFT$value[3], " (", diagrammDFT$value.percent[3],"%) Less than ",Filter.threshold.ms," files identified by MS/MS"),
              paste0(diagrammDFT$value[4], " (", diagrammDFT$value.percent[4],"%) Proteins kept for analysis")),
    value = c(nb_specific, nb_obs, nb_ms, nbProteins)
    ) %>%
    mutate(value.percent = round(.$value / sum(.$value) * 100, 1),
           filter = factor(.$filter, levels = .$filter[1:4]))
  
  # Filtering results bar plot:
  diagramm <- ggplot(diagrammDF, aes(x = "", y = value, fill = filter)) +
    geom_bar(width = .5, stat = "identity") +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette="Blues") +
    xlab("") +
    ylab("") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.title = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 20),
          axis.text.x = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(size=22),
          legend.text = element_text(size=21))

  return(list(filtered_data, mean_abundance_repbio, diagrammDFT, diagramm))
}
```

```{r normalization}

## Normalization by the median of ratios to a reference sample. The normalization factors are computed on the proteins kept ##
## for the analysis, or on the proteins given in Proteins.for.normalization, and applied to all the proteins. ##

if (normalization){

  raw_abundance = data[c("Id",as.character(expDesign$File))]
  kept_rows <- raw_abundance$Id %in% kept_ids

  # Proteins used to compute the normalization factors
  Normalization_list <- Normalization_list[!is.na(Normalization_list)]
  if(length(Normalization_list) > 0){
    normalization_rows <- raw_abundance$Id %in% Normalization_list
    if(!any(normalization_rows)){
      stop("None of the proteins given in Proteins.for.normalization was found in the Id column of the quantification table.")
    }
  }else{
    normalization_rows <- kept_rows
  }

  # Reference sample: the sample with the fewest missing values among the proteins kept for the analysis
  reference_sample = choose_reference_sample(numeric_sample_matrix(raw_abundance[kept_rows, -1]))

  # Normalization (the factors are returned in the "norm_factors" attribute)
  normalized_abundance = normalize(raw_abundance, reference_sample, rows = normalization_rows)
  normalization_factors <- attr(normalized_abundance, "norm_factors")

  # Merging normalized values with data, and creating normalized_abundance var
  data = merge.data.frame(data,normalized_abundance,by="Id")
  normalized_abundance = normalized_abundance[,grepl("_norm",colnames(normalized_abundance))]

  pattern="_norm"
}else{
  pattern=""
}
```

```{r na_distribution, results='asis'}

## Calculating missing values per group ##

# Dataframe storing the median abundance accross bio-reps and number of missing values
na_distribution = data.frame(median=numeric(),sum_na=numeric())

# Dataframe that will store missing value percentages per group
na_percentage = data.frame(Group=character(),na_percentage=character(),na_count=character())

# Looping through each group
for(Group in group_ids){
  
  # Selecting the bio-rep mean abundance columns for this group and adding a check if no mean_abundance found
  current_group_cols <- group_cols(Group, "_mean", colnames(mean_abundance_repbio))

  current_group_intensities <- mean_abundance_repbio[current_group_cols]
  current_group_intensities_nrows = nrow(current_group_intensities)
  
  # Only calculating missing-value summaries if the table contains rows
  if (current_group_intensities_nrows > 0 ) {
    
    # Calculating the percentage of missing values and adding it to the missing values summary
    na_count = sum(is.na(current_group_intensities))
    NA_percentage = na_count/(current_group_intensities_nrows*ncol(current_group_intensities))*100
    na_percentage = rbind(na_percentage,data.frame(Group,NA_percentage,na_count))

    # Adding median and sum_na culumns to the missingness distribution table
    current_group_intensities$median = rowMedians(as.matrix(current_group_intensities),na.rm = T)
    current_group_intensities$sum_na = as.factor(apply(current_group_intensities[-ncol(current_group_intensities)],1,function(x) sum(is.na(x))))
    na_distribution = rbind(na_distribution,current_group_intensities[,(ncol(current_group_intensities)-1):ncol(current_group_intensities)])
  }

}
# Add a final row summarizing across groups
mean_abundance_only <- mean_abundance_repbio[, grepl("_mean$", colnames(mean_abundance_repbio)), drop = FALSE]
na_percentage = rbind(na_percentage, data.frame(Group="All groups",
                                                NA_percentage=sum(is.na(mean_abundance_only))/(nrow(mean_abundance_only)*ncol(mean_abundance_only))*100,
                                                na_count=sum(is.na(mean_abundance_only))))
```

```{r missing_values_imputation, results='asis'}


## Classes of the missing values of the proteins kept for the analysis, per protein and condition (k observed values), on the log2 bio-rep means: ##
## MNAR if k <= Imputation.MNAR.max.obs (imputed below with the background noise); MCAR if k >= Imputation.MCAR.min.obs and the protein is ##
## identified by MS/MS in at least Imputation.MCAR.min.MSMS samples (and, with the intensity criterion, its mean intensity is above the cutoff), ##
## handled according to Imputation.MCAR.model; left missing otherwise. ##

mcar_cells <- NULL
mcar_cutoff <- NULL

# Bio-rep mean intensities (linear and log2), in the order of the rows of data
mean_cols <- group_cols(group_ids, "_mean", colnames(mean_abundance_repbio))
linear_means <- numeric_sample_matrix(mean_abundance_repbio[match(data$Id, mean_abundance_repbio$Id), mean_cols, drop = FALSE])
log_means <- log2_intensity_matrix(data.frame(Id = data$Id, linear_means, check.names = FALSE))
mean_groups <- group_of_cols("_mean")[mean_cols]
mcar_ids <- data$Id
kept_mcar_rows <- mcar_ids %in% kept_ids

# MNAR missing values: proteins with at most Imputation.MNAR.max.obs observed values in the condition
missing_cells <- is.na(log_means) & kept_mcar_rows
mnar_cells <- matrix(FALSE, nrow(log_means), ncol(log_means), dimnames = dimnames(log_means))
for (g in unique(mean_groups)) {
  s <- which(mean_groups == g)
  k <- rowSums(!is.na(log_means[, s, drop = FALSE]))
  mnar_cells[, s] <- missing_cells[, s, drop = FALSE] & (k <= Imputation.MNAR.max.obs)
}

if(imputation_method == "knn"){

  identified_msms <-as.matrix(data[group_cols(group_ids, "_identification_type", names(data))]) == "By MS/MS"

  # Intensity cutoff (estimated on the kept proteins), if the criterion is used
  cutoff_value <- NA
  if (Imputation.MCAR.intensity.cutoff %in% c("auto", "Q1")) {
    # The missing-value rate against the intensity is computed in both cases (shown in the report)
    mcar_cutoff <- estimate_mcar_intensity_cutoff(log_means[kept_mcar_rows, , drop = FALSE], mean_groups)
    if (Imputation.MCAR.intensity.cutoff == "Q1") {
      # Q1: first quartile of all the observed log2 intensities of the kept proteins
      kept_log_values <- log_means[kept_mcar_rows, , drop = FALSE]
      mcar_cutoff$cutoff <- unname(quantile(kept_log_values[!is.na(kept_log_values)], 0.25))
    }
    cutoff_value <- mcar_cutoff$cutoff
  }

  # MCAR missing values
  mcar_cells <- matrix(FALSE, nrow(log_means), ncol(log_means), dimnames = dimnames(log_means))
  mcar_cells[kept_mcar_rows, ] <- classify_mcar(log_means[kept_mcar_rows, , drop = FALSE], mean_groups, identified_msms[kept_mcar_rows, , drop = FALSE],
                                                Imputation.MCAR.min.obs, Imputation.MCAR.min.MSMS, cutoff = cutoff_value)

  # MCAR takes precedence over MNAR (needed when Imputation.MNAR.max.obs has no limit)
  mnar_cells[mcar_cells] <- FALSE

  # MCAR values imputed from the neighbours (the observed values are kept exactly as given)
  mcar_values <- linear_means
  knn_result <- impute_mcar_neighbours(log_means[kept_mcar_rows, , drop = FALSE], mean_groups, mcar_cells[kept_mcar_rows, , drop = FALSE],
                                       Imputation.knn.min.occurrences, seed = 1)
  imputed_part <- mcar_values[kept_mcar_rows, , drop = FALSE]
  mcar_part <- mcar_cells[kept_mcar_rows, , drop = FALSE]
  imputed_part[mcar_part] <- 2^knn_result$values[mcar_part]
  mcar_values[kept_mcar_rows, ] <- imputed_part

  # "_mcar" columns: intensities after the MCAR imputation, used by the MNAR imputation
  mcar_table <- data.frame(Id = data$Id, mcar_values, check.names = FALSE)
  colnames(mcar_table) <- c("Id", sub("_mean$", "_mcar", mean_cols))
  data = merge.data.frame(data, mcar_table, by = "Id")

  # Setting pattern to _mcar for later column finding
  pattern = "_mcar"

}else{

  # If no mcar imputation, set pattern to _mean
  pattern = "_mean"
}

## MNAR IMPUTATION ##

# Intensities to impute (after the MCAR step if any)
intensities_to_impute = data[c("Id", group_cols(group_ids, pattern, colnames(data)))]

# The imputation is done once, on the proteins kept by the global filter: the model is estimated on these proteins only,
# and the other proteins keep their observed values and their missing values
kept_rows <- intensities_to_impute$Id %in% kept_ids
percentile = Imputation.MNAR.percentage/100

# Missing values not imputed by the MNAR imputation: the missing values that are neither MNAR nor MCAR (left missing).
# The MCAR values imputed by knn are no longer missing.
not_mnar_cells <- missing_cells & !mnar_cells
if (imputation_method == "knn") not_mnar_cells <- not_mnar_cells & !mcar_cells
skip_cells <- not_mnar_cells[match(intensities_to_impute$Id, mcar_ids), , drop = FALSE]
if (!any(skip_cells)) skip_cells <- NULL

# Imputing with the noise model ("gaussian") or the percentile model per parameter
if(Imputation.MNAR.model == "gaussian"){

  # Noise model estimated on the kept proteins, then values drawn around the noise level of each sample, with a fixed seed
  # (the model is estimated on the observed values only: the values imputed by the MCAR step are not used)
  sample_groups <- group_of_cols(pattern)[colnames(intensities_to_impute)[-1]]
  estimation_input <- intensities_to_impute
  if (imputation_method == "knn") {
    knn_cells <- mcar_cells[match(estimation_input$Id, mcar_ids), , drop = FALSE]
    estimation_values <- as.matrix(estimation_input[-1]); estimation_values[knn_cells] <- NA
    estimation_input[-1] <- as.data.frame(estimation_values)
  }
  noise_model = estimate_noise_model(estimation_input, sample_groups, percentile, rows = kept_rows)
  imputed_abundance = impute_using_noise_model(intensities_to_impute, sample_groups, noise_model, rows = kept_rows, seed = 1, skip = skip_cells)

}else if(Imputation.MNAR.model == "percentile"){

  imputed_kept = impute_using_noise_percentile(intensities_to_impute[kept_rows, , drop = FALSE],percentile,
                                               skip = if (is.null(skip_cells)) NULL else skip_cells[kept_rows, , drop = FALSE])
  imputed_abundance = intensities_to_impute
  colnames(imputed_abundance) = colnames(imputed_kept)
  imputed_abundance[kept_rows, ] = imputed_kept

}else{
  stop("Unknown Imputation.MNAR.model: '", Imputation.MNAR.model, "' (expected: gaussian or percentile).")
}

# Add imputed abundance columns back to main dataframe
data = merge.data.frame(data,imputed_abundance,by="Id")

# Keep ID column, log transform the rest
imputed_abundance_values <- imputed_abundance[, 2:ncol(imputed_abundance)]

imputed_abundance_values <- data.frame(
  lapply(imputed_abundance_values, as.numeric),
  check.names = FALSE
)

imputed_abundance_values[imputed_abundance_values <= 0] <- NA

imputed_abundance_log <- data.frame(
  Id = imputed_abundance[, 1],
  log10(imputed_abundance_values),
  check.names = FALSE
)

colnames(imputed_abundance_log)[2:ncol(imputed_abundance_log)] <- paste0(
  colnames(imputed_abundance)[2:ncol(imputed_abundance)],
  "_log"
)

data = merge.data.frame(data,imputed_abundance_log,by="Id")

# Make a data frame of values to plot (proteins kept by the global filter)
imputed_abundance_log = data[grepl("_log$|Id$",colnames(data))]
imputationDF = reshape2::melt(imputed_abundance_log[imputed_abundance_log$Id %in% kept_ids,-1])
colnames(imputationDF) = c("Sample","log_abundance")

# Also create a log-transformed version of the original (non-imputed) bio-rep mean abundance table,
# used by the statistical tests and the outputs when imputation is disabled
abundance_log = mean_abundance_repbio
abundance_log[,2:ncol(abundance_log)] = log10(data.matrix(abundance_log[,2:ncol(abundance_log)]))
colnames(abundance_log)[2:ncol(abundance_log)] = paste0(colnames(mean_abundance_repbio)[2:ncol(abundance_log)],"_noimpute_log")

data = merge.data.frame(data,abundance_log,by="Id")
abundance_log = data[c("Id", group_cols(group_ids, "_mean_noimpute_log", colnames(data)))]

# Identifying values that were missing before imputation (same proteins, in the same order)
kept_log_ids <- imputed_abundance_log$Id[imputed_abundance_log$Id %in% kept_ids]
imputed = reshape2::melt(is.na(mean_abundance_repbio[match(kept_log_ids, mean_abundance_repbio$Id),-1]))
imputationDF = cbind(imputationDF,imputed$value)
colnames(imputationDF) = c("Sample","Intensity","Is_imputed")

# Framing of 'Log intensities distribution with imputed values' histogram
histogram <- ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(data = imputationDF, mapping = aes(x = Intensity, fill = Is_imputed), alpha=0.7, bins = 100) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("dodgerblue3", "darkorchid4"))+
  ggtitle("Log intensities distribution with imputed values") +
  xlab("log(intensity)")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size=22),
          axis.title=element_text(size=22),
          axis.text=element_text(size=22),
          legend.text=element_text(size=22),
          legend.title=element_text(size=22))

# Printing 'Log intensities distribution with imputed values' histogram into html document (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters) with download link
if (format_svg) {
  htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(histogram,"Log_intensities_distribution_with_imputed_values", 12, 10))
} else {
  htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(histogram,"Log_intensities_distribution_with_imputed_values", 1600, 600))
}

# Prints the explanation of the imputation model used
if(Imputation.MNAR.model == "gaussian"){
  cat(text_spec(paste0("Missing values of the ", sum(kept_rows), " proteins kept for the analysis were imputed with the noise model. The noise level of each sample is the ",
                       Imputation.MNAR.percentage, "% percentile of its observed intensities (log10: ", formatC(min(noise_model$noise_level)*log10(2), format = "f", digits = 2), " to ",
                       formatC(max(noise_model$noise_level)*log10(2), format = "f", digits = 2), "). For each protein and condition with missing values, values are drawn around these levels with a standard deviation of ",
                       formatC(noise_model$noise_sd, format = "f", digits = 2), " log2 (", formatC(noise_model$noise_sd*log10(2), format = "f", digits = 2),
                       " log10), estimated within conditions on ", noise_model$n_rows, " low-intensity protein/condition measurements. The imputation uses a fixed seed and is reproducible."),italic=T,font_size="12px"))
}else{
  cat(text_spec(paste0("Missing values of the ", sum(kept_rows), " proteins kept for the analysis were replaced by the ", Imputation.MNAR.percentage,
                       "% percentile of the observed intensities of each sample."),italic=T,font_size="12px"))
}
```

```{r mcar_classification, results='asis'}

## Classes of the missing values: missing-value rate against the intensity, intensity cutoff and number of values in each class ##

n_missing_kept <- sum(missing_cells)
n_mnar <- sum(mnar_cells)
n_mcar <- if (is.null(mcar_cells)) 0 else sum(mcar_cells)
n_left <- n_missing_kept - n_mnar - n_mcar

# Summary of the classes (only when some missing values are not imputed with the background noise)
if (imputation_method == "knn" || is.finite(Imputation.MNAR.max.obs)) {
  mnar_rule <- if (is.finite(Imputation.MNAR.max.obs)) paste0("at most ", Imputation.MNAR.max.obs, " observed value(s) in the condition") else "not MCAR"
  cat(text_spec(paste0("Missing values of the proteins kept for the analysis: ", n_missing_kept, ". MNAR (", mnar_rule, "), imputed with the background noise: ", n_mnar,
                       if (imputation_method == "knn") paste0(". MCAR, imputed from the neighbours: ", n_mcar) else "",
                       ". Left missing (tests on the observed values only): ", n_left, "."), italic = T, font_size = "12px"))
  cat(text_spec("\n"))
}

if (imputation_method == "knn") {

  # Missing-value rate against the mean intensity of the protein/condition rows, with the cutoff
  if (!is.null(mcar_cutoff) && !is.null(mcar_cutoff$bins)) {
    bins <- mcar_cutoff$bins
    rate_plot <- ggplot(bins, aes(x = center * log10(2))) +
      geom_point(aes(y = 100 * rate), size = 3, colour = "dodgerblue3") +
      geom_step(aes(y = 100 * fitted), direction = "mid", colour = "dodgerblue4") +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 100 * mcar_cutoff$plateau, linetype = "dotted") +
      {if (is.finite(mcar_cutoff$cutoff)) geom_vline(xintercept = mcar_cutoff$cutoff * log10(2), linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkorchid4")} +
      ggtitle("Missing values against the mean intensity (protein/condition)") +
      xlab("log(mean intensity of the observed values)") + ylab("Missing values (%)") +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size=22), axis.title=element_text(size=20), axis.text=element_text(size=18))
    if (format_svg) {
      cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(rate_plot, "Missing_values_against_intensity", 12, 7)))
    } else {
      cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(rate_plot, "Missing_values_against_intensity", 1200, 700)))
    }
  }

  # Explanation of the classification
  criterion <- paste0("at least ", Imputation.MCAR.min.obs, " observed values and ", Imputation.MCAR.min.MSMS, " MS/MS identifications in the condition")
  if (Imputation.MCAR.intensity.cutoff == "auto") {
    if (is.na(mcar_cutoff$cutoff)) {
      criterion <- paste0(criterion, " (the intensity criterion was not applied: ", mcar_cutoff$message, ")")
    } else if (!is.finite(mcar_cutoff$cutoff)) {
      criterion <- paste0(criterion, " (no intensity dependence of the missing values was found, so the intensity criterion does not exclude any protein)")
    } else {
      criterion <- paste0(criterion, ", and a mean intensity of at least ", formatC(mcar_cutoff$cutoff * log10(2), format = "f", digits = 2),
                          " (log10). This cutoff is the intensity above which the missing-value rate (points; smoothed: line) is within 1 percentage point of its plateau (",
                          formatC(100 * mcar_cutoff$plateau, format = "f", digits = 1), "%, dotted line)")
    }
  } else if (Imputation.MCAR.intensity.cutoff == "Q1") {
    criterion <- paste0(criterion, ", and a mean intensity of at least ", formatC(mcar_cutoff$cutoff * log10(2), format = "f", digits = 2),
                        " (log10), the first quartile of the observed intensities of the proteins kept for the analysis (dashed line)")
  }
  handling <- paste0("They were imputed from the ", knn_result$n_neighbours, " protein/condition rows nearest in intensity (knn model): the values keep the mean of the protein and give it the median standard deviation of its neighbours, corrected for the number of missing values.")
  cat(text_spec(paste0("Missing values classified as MCAR (missing completely at random): ", n_mcar, " of the ", n_missing_kept,
                       " missing values of the proteins kept for the analysis, in protein/condition rows with ", criterion, ". ", handling),
                italic = T, font_size = "12px"))
}
```

```{r compute_cv_distribution, results='asis', message=F}
## Within-group comparison of variation before and after pre-processing/imputation ##

# Initializing output tables, one row per filtered protein
df_median_deviation_before_processing = seq(1,nrow(filtered_data)) #data
df_median_deviation_after_processing = seq(1,nrow(filtered_data)) #data

df_cv_before_processing = seq(1,nrow(filtered_data)) #data
df_cv_after_processing = seq(1,nrow(filtered_data)) #data

# Looping through each experimental group
for (group in group_ids){
  
  # Selecting bio-rep mean abundance columns for group
  before_cols <- group_cols(group, "_mean", names(filtered_data))
  intensities = filtered_data[before_cols]

  # Compute median deviation for the selected group columns
  intensities_median_deviation = compute_median_deviation(intensities)
  colnames(intensities_median_deviation) = rep(group,ncol(intensities_median_deviation))
  
  # Add median deviation and CV values to before-imputation tables
  df_median_deviation_before_processing = cbind(df_median_deviation_before_processing,intensities_median_deviation)
  df_cv_before_processing = cbind(df_cv_before_processing,compute_cv(intensities))

  # Select post-imputation columns for this group
  after_cols <- group_cols(group, paste0(pattern, "_imputed"), names(filtered_data))
  intensities = filtered_data[after_cols]

  # Computing median deviation for the selected group columns
  intensities_median_deviation = compute_median_deviation(intensities)
  colnames(intensities_median_deviation) = rep(group,ncol(intensities_median_deviation))
  
  # Adding median deviation and CV values to after-imputation tables
  df_median_deviation_after_processing = cbind(df_median_deviation_after_processing,intensities_median_deviation)
  df_cv_after_processing = cbind(df_cv_after_processing,compute_cv(intensities))
}
```

```{r biological_error, results='asis'}
## Count extreme biological errors after pre-processing ##

# Initialization as an empty character string
df_cv_after_long$within_boundaries <- NA

# Looping through groups
for (group in group_ids){
  
  # Take a subset of the CV table containing only the current group
  sub = subset(df_cv_after_long,df_cv_after_long$Group==group)
  
  # Calculate the boxplot statistics
  whiskers = boxplot.stats(sub$value)$stats[c(1, 5)]
  max_whisker = whiskers[2]

  # Marking per their relation to the upper whisker (True = at or below, False = above, NA stays NA)
  df_cv_after_long$within_boundaries[df_cv_after_long$Group==group & df_cv_after_long$value <= max_whisker] <- TRUE
  df_cv_after_long$within_boundaries[df_cv_after_long$Group==group & df_cv_after_long$value > max_whisker] <- FALSE
  df_cv_after_long$within_boundaries[df_cv_after_long$Group==group & is.na(df_cv_after_long$value)] <- NA
}

# Keeping only values that were set to False (above the upper whisker)
df_cv_after_processing_outliers = subset(df_cv_after_long, df_cv_after_long$within_boundaries==F)

# Plotting a bar plot showing the extreme CV values/outliers detected within each group
```

```{r pval_calculation_anova_kruskall, results='asis'}

## Pvalue calculation for Anova/Kruskall ##

# Returns the filtering of a comparison (filter_dataset applied to the two conditions only): [[1]] filtered data, [[2]] bio-rep mean abundances
comparison_filter <- function(A_name, B_name){

  # Starting a comparison-specific filtering table with identifier columns
  filtering_data <- data[c("Id", "Accession", "Gene_name", "Label", "Specific_peptides")]

  # Add abundance and identification columns for each of the comparison groups
  for(group in c(A_name, B_name)){

    # Adding the mean abundance columns of the group to the filtering table
    group_mean_cols <- group_cols(group, "_mean", colnames(global_mean_abundance_repbio))
    sel_global_mean_abundance_repbio <- global_mean_abundance_repbio %>% select(Id, all_of(group_mean_cols))
    filtering_data <- filtering_data %>% left_join(sel_global_mean_abundance_repbio,by="Id")

    # For each raw file in this group, add raw intensity column and matching identification type column
    for(file in expDesign[expDesign$Condition == group,]$File){
      filtering_data <- cbind(filtering_data, data[file])
      filtering_data <- cbind(filtering_data, data[paste0("Identification_type", sub("Intensity", "", file))])
    }
  }

  # Add all log-transformed abundance columns
  filtering_data <- cbind(filtering_data, data[grepl("_log$", colnames(data))])

  filter_dataset(filtering_data, c(A_name, B_name))
}

# Clear pvalue_table
pvalue_table <- NULL

if(Test.type %in% c("anova","kruskall")){
  
  # If imputation is used, take logged or unlogged imputed values. Else, take unimputed logged or unlogged values
  # (col_suffix is the suffix of the per-sample columns of the selected table)
  if(imputation){
    if(Test.log==T){
      intensity_df = imputed_abundance_log
      col_suffix = paste0(pattern, "_imputed_log")
    }else{
      intensity_df = imputed_abundance
      col_suffix = paste0(pattern, "_imputed")
    }
  }else{
    if(Test.log==T){
      intensity_df = abundance_log
      col_suffix = "_mean_noimpute_log"
    }else{
      intensity_df = mean_abundance_repbio
      col_suffix = "_mean"
    }
  }
  intensity_df = intensity_df[c("Id", group_cols(group_ids, col_suffix, colnames(intensity_df)))]

  # Reshape intensity_df to anova test input (each row is one measurement and "variable" stores the group of the sample)
  reshape_abundance = reshape2::melt(intensity_df,id="Id")
  reshape_abundance$variable = unname(group_of_cols(col_suffix)[as.character(reshape_abundance$variable)])
  
  # Tukey p-value of a comparison "A/B" (rows of the Tukey table named "B-A" or "A-B"); NA if the pair is absent
  tukey_pvalue <- function(tab, A_name, B_name){
    p <- tab[c(paste0(A_name, "-", B_name), paste0(B_name, "-", A_name))]
    p <- p[!is.na(p)]
    if (length(p) == 0) NA_real_ else unname(p[1])
  }
  comparison_pairs <- strsplit(comparisons_to_display, "/")

  # Proteins tested in each comparison: those passing the filter of the comparison (the post-hoc correction of a protein
  # is computed over the comparisons in which it is tested)
  tested_in_comparison <- sapply(comparison_pairs, function(ab) kept_ids %in% comparison_filter(ab[1], ab[2])[[1]]$Id)
  if (is.null(dim(tested_in_comparison))) tested_in_comparison <- matrix(tested_in_comparison, ncol = length(comparison_pairs))
  rownames(tested_in_comparison) <- as.character(kept_ids)

  # For each protein kept for the analysis, run the global test and the pairwise tests of the comparisons
  # (a protein that cannot be tested, e.g. with too few values, gets NA p-values instead of stopping the report)
  tested_ids <- intersect(unique(reshape_abundance$Id), kept_ids)
  observed_long <- reshape_abundance[!is.na(reshape_abundance$value), ]
  by_protein <- split(observed_long, observed_long$Id)
  n_cmp <- length(comparison_pairs)
  pvalue_rows <- lapply(tested_ids, function(id){

    # Keeping only the observed or imputed abundance values of the current protein
    current <- by_protein[[as.character(id)]]
    if (is.null(current)) return(rep(NA_real_, 2 * n_cmp + 1))
    current$variable <- factor(current$variable)
    tested <- tested_in_comparison[as.character(id), ]

    result <- tryCatch({

      # Global test over all the conditions
      if(Test.type=="anova"){
        anova = aov(value ~ variable, data = current)
        pval = summary(anova)[[1]][[1,"Pr(>F)"]]
      }else{
        pval = kruskal.test(value ~ variable, data = current)$p.value
      }

      # Raw p-values of the comparisons in which the protein is tested: test of the two conditions of each comparison
      # (t-test after an anova, Wilcoxon after a Kruskal-Wallis test)
      raw <- sapply(seq_len(n_cmp), function(j){
        if (!tested[j]) return(NA_real_)
        a <- current$value[current$variable == comparison_pairs[[j]][1]]
        b <- current$value[current$variable == comparison_pairs[[j]][2]]
        tryCatch(if(Test.type=="anova") t.test(a, b, var.equal = Test.var.equal)$p.value else wilcox.test(a, b)$p.value,
                 error = function(e) NA_real_)
      })

      # Post-hoc p-values
      if(Test.posthoc.procedure=="tukey"){

        # Tukey: all the pairs of conditions, with the residual variance pooled over all the conditions
        tukey <- TukeyHSD(x=anova, "variable", conf.level=1-Stat.threshold.significance)$variable[, "p adj"]
        pairwise <- sapply(comparison_pairs, function(ab) tukey_pvalue(tukey, ab[1], ab[2]))
        pairwise[!tested] <- NA

      }else{

        # Holm or Bonferroni: correction over the comparisons in which the protein is tested (none: raw p-values)
        pairwise <- raw
        if (Test.posthoc.procedure != "none") pairwise[!is.na(raw)] <- p.adjust(raw[!is.na(raw)], method = Test.posthoc.procedure)
      }
      c(pval, raw, pairwise)
    }, error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, 2 * n_cmp + 1))

    result
  })
  pvalue_table <- data.frame(Id = tested_ids, do.call(rbind, pvalue_rows), check.names = FALSE)
  colnames(pvalue_table) <- c("Id", "global_pval", paste0("raw_", comparisons_to_display), comparisons_to_display)

  # Gating by the global test (Test.anova.gating=bh): the pairwise comparisons are only kept for the proteins whose global test passes
  # the significance threshold after a BH correction across proteins; the other proteins get no post-hoc p-value (and no q-value)
  gated_ids <- pvalue_table$Id
  if (Test.anova.gating == "bh") {
    global_q <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(pvalue_table)); defined <- !is.na(pvalue_table$global_pval)
    global_q[defined] <- p.adjust(pvalue_table$global_pval[defined], method = "BH")
    gated <- !is.na(global_q) & global_q <= Stat.threshold.significance
    pvalue_table[!gated, comparisons_to_display] <- NA
    gated_ids <- pvalue_table$Id[gated]
    cat(text_spec(paste0("\nGating by the global test (", if (Test.type == "anova") "anova" else "Kruskal-Wallis", "): ", sum(gated), " of ", sum(defined),
                         " proteins have a global q-value (BH) of at most ", Stat.threshold.significance,
                         "; the comparisons are tested and corrected on these proteins only.",
                         if (length(group_ids) < 5) paste0(" Warning: with ", length(group_ids), " conditions, this gating can make the false discovery rate of each comparison exceed its nominal level (about 6% instead of 5% in a simulation with 3 conditions).") else ""),
                  italic = T, font_size = "12px"))
  }
}
```
