```{r DA, results='asis'}

 #########################################################Pairwise statistics #########################################################

# Initializing the starting statistics table containing one protein per row
statDF = data.frame(filtered_data$Id,filtered_data$Accession,filtered_data$Label) #data
colnames(statDF) = c("Id","Accession","Label")

# Clean copy of identifier only DF
precv_statDF <- statDF

# Creating main output table, adding globally imputed abundance values by Id
output_t <- data[c("Id", "Accession", "Gene_name", "Label", "Specific_peptides")]
output_t <- dplyr::left_join(output_t, global_imputed_abundance, by = "Id")

# Statistic computing for each pairwise condition comparison
for (comparison in comparisons_to_display){
  
  # Splitting comparison string into 2 condition names
  couple = strsplit(comparison,"/")[[1]]
  A_name = couple[1]
  B_name = couple[2]
  
  # Apply filtering to only the two conditions for comparison
  cond_fltr <- comparison_filter(A_name, B_name)

  # Extract filtered outputs
  filtered_data <- as.data.frame(cond_fltr[[1]])
  mean_abundance_repbio <- as.data.frame(cond_fltr[[2]])

  # Keep only imputed abundance rows that passed the comparison-specific filter
  imputed_abundance <- global_imputed_abundance[global_imputed_abundance$Id %in% filtered_data$Id, ]
  
  #################################### Biolding intensity tables for comparison groups #########################################################

  # Paired test: the pairs of replicates used for this comparison
  if (Test.paired) cat(text_spec(paste0("\n", paired_text(A_name, B_name)), italic = T, font_size = "12px"))
  
  # Using imputed or non-imputed DFs depending on parameters
  if (imputation) {
    
    A_cols <- group_cols(A_name, paste0(pattern, "_imputed"), colnames(imputed_abundance))
    B_cols <- group_cols(B_name, paste0(pattern, "_imputed"), colnames(imputed_abundance))
    if (Test.paired) B_cols <- B_cols[paired_order(A_name, B_name)]

    A <- data.frame(Accession = filtered_data$Accession, Label = filtered_data$Label, imputed_abundance[A_cols], check.names = FALSE)
    B <- data.frame(Accession = filtered_data$Accession, Label = filtered_data$Label, imputed_abundance[B_cols], check.names = FALSE)
    
  } else {
    
    A_cols <- group_cols(A_name, "_mean", colnames(mean_abundance_repbio))
    B_cols <- group_cols(B_name, "_mean", colnames(mean_abundance_repbio))
    if (Test.paired) B_cols <- B_cols[paired_order(A_name, B_name)]

    A <- data.frame(Accession = filtered_data$Accession, Label = filtered_data$Label, mean_abundance_repbio[A_cols], check.names = FALSE)
    B <- data.frame(Accession = filtered_data$Accession, Label = filtered_data$Label, mean_abundance_repbio[B_cols], check.names = FALSE)
    
  }
  
  # Merging conditions A and B by protein identifiers
  totIntensities = merge.data.frame(A,B,by=c("Accession","Label"))
  
  # Calculate the average intensity across all intensity columns from both conditions
  totIntensities[paste0("mean_intensity_",comparison)] = rowMeans(data.matrix(totIntensities[,3:ncol(totIntensities)]), na.rm=T)
  
  #################################### Computing Fold Change #########################################################
  
  # If using a paired test (fc calculated differently)
  if(Test.paired){
    
    # Calculate paired ratios for each paired replicate, converting them to log 2 space, averaging the log2 ratios and then converting them back to fold-change scale
    paired_ratios <- data.matrix(totIntensities[A_cols]) / data.matrix(totIntensities[B_cols])
    paired_ratios[paired_ratios <= 0] <- NA
    log_paired_ratios = log2(paired_ratios)
    totIntensities[paste0("fc_",comparison)] = 2^(rowMeans(log_paired_ratios))
    
  }else{
    
    # For unpaired comparisons, average the A and B columns selected above
    # (imputed "_mean_imputed" / "_mcar_imputed" columns, or "_mean" columns without imputation)
    totIntensities[paste0("mean_intensity_",A_name)] = rowMeans(data.matrix(totIntensities[A_cols]),na.rm = TRUE)
    totIntensities[paste0("mean_intensity_",B_name)] = rowMeans(data.matrix(totIntensities[B_cols]),na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Calculating fold change as A / B
    totIntensities[paste0("fc_",comparison)] = totIntensities[paste0("mean_intensity_",A_name)] / totIntensities[paste0("mean_intensity_",B_name)]
  }
  
  # Adding fc results to statDF
  statDF = merge.data.frame(precv_statDF,totIntensities[,c("Accession",paste0("mean_intensity_",comparison),paste0("fc_",comparison))],by="Accession")

 ######################################################### Compute pvalues #########################################################

  # Rank tests (Wilcoxon, pairwise Wilcoxon after Kruskal-Wallis): with few replicates, the smallest possible p-value can be too large
  # to pass a multiple testing correction
  if(Test.type %in% c("wilcoxon", "kruskall")){
    n_A <- length(A_cols); n_B <- length(B_cols)
    min_p <- if (Test.paired && Test.type == "wilcoxon") 2 / 2^n_A else 2 / choose(n_A + n_B, n_A)
    if (Test.type == "wilcoxon" && alternative != "two.sided") min_p <- min_p / 2
    cat(text_spec(paste0("\nNote (", comparison, "): with ", n_A, " and ", n_B, " values, the smallest p-value the Wilcoxon test can give is ",
                         formatC(min_p, format = "g", digits = 3), if (Test.adjust.procedure != "none") ", before the multiple testing correction" else "", "."),
                  italic = T, font_size = "12px"))
  }

  # If pvalue_table exists and is not NULL, use the previously calculated Anova/Kruskal pvalues
  if(!is.null(pvalue_table)){
    
    # Merging the p-values of this comparison: raw p-values of the pairwise test (pval_) and post-hoc p-values (posthoc_pval_,
    # NA for the proteins not gated by the global test with Test.anova.gating=bh)
    pval_cols <- c("Id", paste0("raw_", comparison), comparison)

    if (!all(pval_cols %in% colnames(pvalue_table))) {
      stop("Missing expected p-value columns: ", paste(setdiff(pval_cols, colnames(pvalue_table)), collapse = ", "))
    }

    statDF <- merge.data.frame(statDF, pvalue_table[pval_cols], by = "Id")
    colnames(statDF)[(ncol(statDF) - 1):ncol(statDF)] <- c(paste0("pval_", comparison), paste0("posthoc_pval_", comparison))
    
  # Else, do a T, Wilcoxon, or Limma test
  }else{
    
    # If the test should be performed on logged values, rebuild A and B accordingly
    if(Test.log==T){
      log_suffix <- if(imputation) paste0(pattern, "_imputed_log") else "_mean_noimpute_log"
      A_cols <- group_cols(A_name, log_suffix, colnames(filtered_data))
      B_cols <- group_cols(B_name, log_suffix, colnames(filtered_data))
      if (Test.paired) B_cols <- B_cols[paired_order(A_name, B_name)]

      A <- data.frame(Accession = filtered_data$Accession, Label = filtered_data$Label, filtered_data[A_cols], check.names = FALSE)
      B <- data.frame(Accession = filtered_data$Accession, Label = filtered_data$Label, filtered_data[B_cols], check.names = FALSE)
    }

    # Do the statistical test
    if(Test.type=="limma"){
      
      # Performing Limma test
      if(Test.paired){

        # Paired design: the pair (replicate) is a factor; the columns of B are in the order of the replicates of A (see paired_order)
        pair <- factor(c(seq_len(ncol(A)-2), seq_len(ncol(B)-2)))
        group <- factor(c(rep(1,ncol(A)-2), rep(2,ncol(B)-2)))
        design <- model.matrix(~group + pair)
        colnames(design)[1:2] <- c("Intercept", "B-A")
      }else{
        
        # Unpaired design
        design <- model.matrix(~factor(c(rep(1,length(A)-2), rep(2,length(B)-2))))
        colnames(design) <- c("Intercept", "B-A")
      }
    
      # Building Limma input matrix from A and B columns
      data_limma<- cbind(A[,3:ncol(A)],B[,3:ncol(B)])
      
      # If accessions are unique, use directly as row names, Else append Id to duplicated accessions to make them unique
      if(sum(isUnique(filtered_data$Accession)) == length(filtered_data$Accession)){
        rownames(data_limma)=filtered_data$Accession
      }else{
        unique_rownames <- filtered_data %>%
          mutate(rowname = ifelse(duplicated(Accession) | duplicated(Accession, fromLast = TRUE),
                            paste(Accession, Id, sep = "_"),
                            Accession)) %>%
          remove_rownames() %>%
          column_to_rownames(var = "rowname")
        row.names(data_limma) <- row.names(unique_rownames)
        }
    
      # Fit Limma model and apply empirical Bayes moderation
      fit <- lmFit(data_limma, design)
      fit <- eBayes(fit)
  
      # Extract all Limma results
      alllimma<-topTable(fit, coef=2, number=Inf, sort.by="none")
  
      # Extracting Limma pvalues and adding them to statDF
      alllimma$Accession = row.names(alllimma)
      statDF = merge.data.frame(statDF,alllimma[grep("Accession|P.Value",colnames(alllimma))],by="Accession")
      colnames(statDF)[ncol(statDF)] = paste0("pval_",comparison)
  
    # T.test / Wilcoxon test
    }else{
      
      # Initialize pvalue column for comparison
      statDF[paste0("pval_",comparison)] <- NA_real_

      # Vectorized two-sample equal-variance t-test (most common case), equivalent to t.test(var.equal = TRUE)
      if(Test.type=="t.test" && Test.var.equal && !Test.paired){

        mat_a <- data.matrix(A[, 3:ncol(A)])
        mat_b <- data.matrix(B[, 3:ncol(B)])

        n_a <- rowSums(!is.na(mat_a))
        n_b <- rowSums(!is.na(mat_b))
        mean_a <- rowMeans(mat_a, na.rm = TRUE)
        mean_b <- rowMeans(mat_b, na.rm = TRUE)
        var_a <- rowSums((mat_a - mean_a)^2, na.rm = TRUE) / (n_a - 1)
        var_b <- rowSums((mat_b - mean_b)^2, na.rm = TRUE) / (n_b - 1)

        # Pooled variance (a group with a single value contributes no variance)
        df <- n_a + n_b - 2
        sp2 <- (ifelse(n_a > 1, (n_a - 1) * var_a, 0) + ifelse(n_b > 1, (n_b - 1) * var_b, 0)) / df
        stderr <- sqrt(sp2 * (1/n_a + 1/n_b))
        t_stat <- (mean_a - mean_b) / stderr

        pvals <- switch(alternative,
          "two.sided" = 2 * pt(-abs(t_stat), df),
          "greater"   = pt(t_stat, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
          "less"      = pt(t_stat, df)
        )

        # Same cases where t.test() stops with an error: an empty group, fewer than 3 values in total, or constant data
        not_testable <- n_a < 1 | n_b < 1 | df < 1 | stderr < 10 * .Machine$double.eps * pmax(abs(mean_a), abs(mean_b))
        pvals[not_testable %in% TRUE] <- NA

        # Add proteins pvalues to statDF
        statDF[paste0("pval_",comparison)] <- pvals[match(statDF$Accession, A[,1])]

      }else{

        # Loop over each protein and apply selected test (Welch, paired or Wilcoxon)
        for(prot in seq_len(nrow(A))){

          # A protein that cannot be tested (e.g. no value in a group, constant data) gets a NA pvalue instead of stopping the report
          pval <- tryCatch({

            # T.Test
            if(Test.type=="t.test"){
              t.test(as.numeric(A[prot,3:ncol(A)]),as.numeric(B[prot,3:ncol(B)]),
                     alternative = alternative,
                     paired=Test.paired,
                     var.equal=Test.var.equal)$p.value

            # Wilcoxon test
            }else if(Test.type=="wilcoxon"){
              wilcox.test(as.numeric(A[prot,3:ncol(A)]),as.numeric(B[prot,3:ncol(B)]),
                          alternative = alternative,
                          paired=Test.paired)$p.value
            }else{
              NA_real_
            }
          }, error = function(e) NA_real_)

          # Add proteins pvalue to statDF
          statDF[paste0("pval_",comparison)][match(A[prot,1],statDF$Accession,nomatch =0),]<- pval
        }
      }

    }
    
  }
  
 ######################################################### Multiple testing correction ######################################################### 
  
  # P-values used for significance: the post-hoc p-values with anova / kruskall, the p-values of the test otherwise
  test_p_prefix <- if (paste0("posthoc_pval_", comparison) %in% colnames(statDF)) "posthoc_pval" else "pval"

  # If an adjustment procedure was selected
  if(Test.adjust.procedure!="none"){

    # Significance evaluated using adjusted pvalues (proteins without p-value, e.g. not gated, get no q-value)
    value="qval"
    test_p <- as.numeric(unlist(statDF[paste0(test_p_prefix,"_",comparison)]))
    qval = rep(NA_real_, nrow(statDF))
    if (any(!is.na(test_p))) {
      procedure_results = mt.rawp2adjp(test_p[!is.na(test_p)], proc=Test.adjust.procedure, alpha=Stat.threshold.significance)
      qval[!is.na(test_p)] = data.frame(procedure_results$adjp,procedure_results$index)[order(procedure_results$index),2]
    }
  }else{

    # Significance will be evaluated based on raw pvalues (post-hoc p-values with anova / kruskall)
    value=test_p_prefix
    qval = rep(NA,nrow(statDF))
  }
  
  # Add adjusted pvalues to the statistics table
  statDF[paste0("qval_",comparison)] = qval
  
  ########################## Significant proteins ##########################
  
  # Ensure statistical result columns are numeric
  stat_cols <- grep("^(mean_intensity_|fc_|pval_|posthoc_pval_|qval_)", colnames(statDF), value = TRUE)
  statDF[stat_cols] <- lapply(statDF[stat_cols], as.numeric)
  statDF[paste0("significant_",comparison)]<-rep(F, nrow(statDF))
  
  # Initially classify every protein as not significant
  statDF[paste0("significant_",comparison)][(statDF[paste0(value,"_",comparison)]<=Stat.threshold.significance)
                                            & (abs(log2(statDF[paste0("fc_",comparison)]))>=Stat.threshold.fc)] <- T
  
  ########################## Results displaying ##########################
  
  # Only results from comparisons specified by the user
  if(comparison%in%comparisons_to_display){
    
    # Extracting columns needed for comparison (the p-values shown are the post-hoc p-values with anova / kruskall)
    current_statDF <- statDF[c("Id","Accession","Label", paste0("mean_intensity_", comparison), paste0("fc_", comparison), paste0(test_p_prefix, "_", comparison), paste0("qval_", comparison), paste0("significant_", comparison))]
    colnames(current_statDF) = c("Id","Accession","Label","mean_intensity","fc","pval","qval","significant")
    
    # Printing comparison name
    cat(text_spec(comparison, color="#3686D5", bold=T, font_size=18 ))
    
    # Printing filtering summary table for comparison
    cat(kable(cond_fltr[[3]], format="html", col.names = c("Filter", "Value", "Value_Percentage"), booktabs = T, caption = "Filtered Proteins") %>%
            kable_styling(bootstrap_options="condensed",full_width = F,position = "center") %>%
            column_spec(1, bold = T))
    
    # Coloring of points (monochrome, by significance, or by intensity)
    if(Vol_colors == "significance"){
      col_sig <- TRUE
      monochrome <- FALSE
    }else if(Vol_colors == "intensity"){
      col_sig <- FALSE
      monochrome <- FALSE
    }else{
      col_sig <- FALSE
      monochrome <- TRUE
    }
      
    # Protein labeling in plot (none, specified list, automatic labeling)
    if(Vol_no_lab == T){
      prtn_lbl_lst <- ""
      lblng_mnl <- TRUE
    }else if(length(Vol_labels) > 0){
      prtn_lbl_lst <- Vol_labels
      lblng_mnl <- TRUE
    }else{
      lblng_mnl <- FALSE
    }
      
    # Setting colors and point sizes to be used
    sig_list <- c('black', 'red')
    col_list <- c('green4', 'yellow3', 'red3')
    pnt_sz <- 1.5
    
      
  ########################## Framing of MA plot using ggplot   ########################## 
    
    # Setting Current_statDF to only contain proteins with valid values
    current_statDF_MA <- current_statDF[!is.na(current_statDF$mean_intensity) &!is.na(current_statDF$fc) &is.finite(current_statDF$mean_intensity) &
      is.finite(current_statDF$fc) & current_statDF$mean_intensity > 0 & current_statDF$fc > 0,]
  
    #Selecting the top 50 most significant proteins with the smallest pvalues
    top_50_pval = current_statDF_MA %>% filter(significant==TRUE) %>% slice_min(pval, n = 50)
    
    # Creating MA plot with ggplot
    MA = ggplot(current_statDF_MA, aes(x=log10(mean_intensity), y=log2(fc))) +
      # Coloring by significance
      {if(col_sig) geom_point(aes(color=significant, alpha = current_statDF_MA$pval),size=ifelse(current_statDF_MA$significant, 2, 1.5))}+
      {if(!col_sig) geom_point(aes(color=-log10(pval), alpha = .7),size=pnt_sz)}+
      {if(col_sig) scale_color_manual(values = sig_list)}+
      # If monochrome coloring
      {if(monochrome && !col_sig) scale_color_gradient(low = 'lightblue', high = 'blue4')}+
      # If coloring by intensity
      {if(!monochrome && !col_sig) scale_color_gradientn(colors = col_list, values = c(0, .5, 1))}+
      # automatic labeling of top 50 proteins by significance (manual labeling is not enabled)
      {if(!lblng_mnl) ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = top_50_pval,aes(label=as.character(top_50_pval$Label)),
                                              hjust=1,vjust=-1, size=3, box.padding = .15,max.overlaps = 10)}+
      {if(!lblng_mnl) labs(subtitle = "Top 50 significant hits were labeled.")} +
      # Manually labeling by accession number
      {if(lblng_mnl) ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = ifelse(current_statDF_MA$Accession %in% prtn_lbl_lst, as.character(current_statDF_MA$Label),'')), 
                                              hjust=1,vjust=-1, size=3, box.padding = .15, max.overlaps = 10000)}+
      # Stat.threshold.fc is already expressed as a log2 fold change
      geom_hline(yintercept=Stat.threshold.fc,linetype="dashed") +
      geom_hline(yintercept=-Stat.threshold.fc,linetype="dashed") +
      ggtitle("MA plot")+
      xlab("log 10(Intensity)")+
      ylab("log2(fc)") +
      theme(legend.position = "right",
        plot.title = element_text(size=22),
        axis.title=element_text(size=24),
        axis.text=element_text(size=22),
        legend.text=element_text(size=16),
        plot.margin = unit(c(2,0,2,0), "cm"),
        legend.title=element_text(size=18)) +
      annotate("text", x = max(log10(current_statDF_MA$mean_intensity), na.rm = TRUE), y = min(log2(current_statDF_MA$fc), na.rm = TRUE),
             label = couple[2], hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 6, font_face = "bold") +
      annotate("text", x = max(log10(current_statDF_MA$mean_intensity), na.rm = TRUE), y = max(log2(current_statDF_MA$fc), na.rm = TRUE),
             label = couple[1], hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 6, font_face = "bold")
    
    # Adding a line break after the plot
    cat(text_spec("\n"))
    
  ########################## Graph Parameters   ########################## 
    
    # P-value at which the volcano plot threshold line is drawn. With a multiple-testing correction, significance is decided
    # on the q-values, so the line is drawn at the largest p-value among the proteins with q <= threshold (no line if there is none).
    # A local variable is used: Stat.threshold.significance must not be modified, as it decides significance for every comparison.
    volcano_pvalue_line <- Stat.threshold.significance
    if(Test.adjust.procedure!="none"){
      significant_df <- subset(current_statDF, !is.na(qval) & qval <= Stat.threshold.significance)
      volcano_pvalue_line <- if (nrow(significant_df) > 0) max(significant_df$pval, na.rm = TRUE) else NA
    }
    
    # Remove rows where either fc or pval is NA
    cstat_noNA <- current_statDF[!is.na(current_statDF$fc) & !is.na(current_statDF$pval) & !is.na(current_statDF$mean_intensity) & is.finite(current_statDF$fc) &
      is.finite(current_statDF$pval) & is.finite(current_statDF$mean_intensity) & current_statDF$fc > 0 & current_statDF$pval > 0 & current_statDF$mean_intensity > 0,]
    
    # Setting coloring scheme (if colored by significance or intensity)
    if(col_sig){
      Significance <- cstat_noNA$significant
      Intensity <- log10(cstat_noNA$mean_intensity)
    }else{
      Intensity <- log10(cstat_noNA$mean_intensity)
    }
    
    # Creating a base volcano plot
    Volcano = ggplot(cstat_noNA, aes(x=log2(fc), y=-log10(as.numeric(cstat_noNA$pval))))
    
    # Modifying volcano plot
    Volcano = Volcano +
      # If coloring by significance
      {if(col_sig) geom_point(aes(color=cstat_noNA$significant, alpha = Intensity),size=ifelse(cstat_noNA$significant, 1.5, 1))}+
      # If not coloring by significance
      {if(!col_sig) geom_point(aes(color=Intensity, alpha = .7),size=pnt_sz)}+
      # Adding pvalue and fc threshold lines
      {if(!is.na(volcano_pvalue_line)) geom_hline(yintercept=-log10(volcano_pvalue_line),linetype="dashed")}+
      # Stat.threshold.fc is already expressed as a log2 fold change
      geom_vline(xintercept=Stat.threshold.fc,linetype="dashed")+
      geom_vline(xintercept=-Stat.threshold.fc,linetype="dashed")+
      # If monochrome mode selected
      {if(monochrome && !col_sig) scale_color_gradient(low = 'lightblue', high = 'blue4')}+
      # If no color scheme, color by intensity
      {if(!monochrome && !col_sig) scale_color_gradientn(colors = col_list, values = c(0, .5, 1))}+
      # If coloring by significance
      {if(col_sig) scale_color_manual(values = sig_list)}+
      # Automatically labeling significant proteins
      {if(!lblng_mnl) ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label=ifelse(cstat_noNA$significant==T,as.character(cstat_noNA$Label),'')),
                                              hjust=1,vjust=-1, size=3, box.padding = .15,max.overlaps = 15)}+
      # If manual labeling, label based on list of accession labels
      {if(lblng_mnl) ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = ifelse(cstat_noNA$Accession %in% prtn_lbl_lst, as.character(cstat_noNA$Label),'')), 
                                              hjust=1,vjust=-1, size=3, box.padding = .15, max.overlaps = 10000)}+
      ggtitle("")+
      xlab(paste0("log2(FC)"))+ 
      ylab(paste0('-log10(pval)'))+
      labs(color='log10(Intensity)') +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(size=22),
            axis.title=element_text(size=18),
            axis.text=element_text(size=18),
            legend.text=element_text(size=16),
            plot.margin = unit(c(2,0,2,0), "cm"),
            legend.title=element_text(size=18)) +
      # Adding group labels
      annotate("text", x = min(log2(cstat_noNA$fc), na.rm = TRUE), y = max(-log10(as.numeric(cstat_noNA$pval)), na.rm = TRUE),
             label = couple[2], hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 6, font_face = "bold") +
      annotate("text", x = max(log2(cstat_noNA$fc), na.rm = TRUE), y = max(-log10(as.numeric(cstat_noNA$pval)), na.rm = TRUE),
             label = couple[1], hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 6, font_face = "bold")
    
    # Plotting and printing of Volcano plot into html (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters) with download link
    if (format_svg) {
      cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(Volcano,"Volcano", 12, 12)))
    } else {
      cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(Volcano,"Volcano", 1200, 1200)))
    }
    
    # Plotting and printing MA plot into html doc (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters) with download link
    if (format_svg) {
      cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(MA,"MA_plot", 12, 12)))
    } else {
      cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(MA,"MA_plot", 1200, 800)))
    }
    
  ########################## Volcano comparisons   ########################## 
    
    cat(text_spec("\n"))
  
  ########################## Creating data frame for heatmap  ########################## 
  
    # Only create the significant-protein heatmap if there is more than one significant protein
    if(length(current_statDF$significant[current_statDF$significant==T])>1){
      
        # Extract rows from current_statDF that were classified as significant
        significant_proteins <- subset(current_statDF, significant == TRUE)
        
        # Match significant proteins back to filtered_data by Id, preserving order
        matched_rows <- match(
          as.character(significant_proteins$Id),
          as.character(filtered_data$Id)
        )
        
        # Remove unmatched rows, if any
        matched_rows <- matched_rows[!is.na(matched_rows)]
        
        significant_proteins_data <- filtered_data[matched_rows, ]

        # Log intensity columns of the A and B samples, in table order
        log_suffix <- if (imputation) paste0(pattern, "_imputed_log") else "_mean_noimpute_log"
        intensity_cols <- intersect(
          names(significant_proteins_data),
          group_cols(c(A_name, B_name), log_suffix, names(significant_proteins_data))
        )

        significant_proteins_intensities <- significant_proteins_data[
          c("Accession", "Label", intensity_cols)
        ]

        # Renaming heatmap columns with the sample ids (column names without their suffix)
        colnames(significant_proteins_intensities) <- c(
          "Accession",
          "Label",
          substr(intensity_cols, 1, nchar(intensity_cols) - nchar(log_suffix))
        )
        
        heatmap_values <- significant_proteins_intensities[, -c(1, 2)]

        heatmap_values <- data.frame(
          lapply(heatmap_values, as.numeric),
          check.names = FALSE
        )
        
        keep_rows <- complete.cases(heatmap_values) &
          apply(heatmap_values, 1, function(x) all(is.finite(as.numeric(x))))
        
        significant_proteins_intensities <- significant_proteins_intensities[keep_rows, ]
        significant_proteins_data <- significant_proteins_data[keep_rows, ]
        
        # Store the sample and group names used in the heatmap
        samples_names_comparison <- colnames(significant_proteins_intensities)[3:ncol(significant_proteins_intensities)]
        group_ids_comparison <- c(A_name, B_name)
        
        raw_mean_cols <- paste0(samples_names_comparison, "_mean")
        
        missing_raw_cols <- setdiff(raw_mean_cols, colnames(significant_proteins_data))
        
        if (length(missing_raw_cols) > 0) {
          stop(
            "Missing raw mean columns for imputed mask: ",
            paste(missing_raw_cols, collapse = ", ")
          )
        }
        
        raw_intensities_significant_proteins <- significant_proteins_data[
          c("Id", "Accession", "Label", raw_mean_cols)
        ]
        
        # Build imputed mask in the structure expected by create_heatmap()
        # Important: create_heatmap() looks for mask columns containing "mean"
        imputed <- data.frame(
          raw_intensities_significant_proteins[, c("Accession", "Label")],
          is.na(raw_intensities_significant_proteins[, raw_mean_cols, drop = FALSE]),
          check.names = FALSE
        )
        
        # create_heatmap() expects the first identifier column to be named "Id"
        # In this heatmap context, this "Id" is actually the row identifier used for plotting,
        # so we use Accession here to match significant_proteins_intensities.
        colnames(imputed)[1:2] <- c("Id", "Label")
        
        # Keep the original raw mean column names, because create_heatmap() uses contains("mean")
        colnames(imputed)[-(1:2)] <- raw_mean_cols
                
  ########################## Framing 'Heatmap' plot  ########################## 
        
        if (nrow(significant_proteins_intensities) >= 2) {
          
          heatmap_plot <- create_heatmap(
            significant_proteins_intensities,
            imputed,
            samples_names_comparison,
            group_ids_comparison,
            "Log Intensities Heatmap"
          )
  
          # Plotting and printing 'Heatmap' plot into html doc (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters) with download link
          if (format_svg) {
            cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(heatmap_plot,"Heatmap", 15, 15)))
          } else {
            cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(heatmap_plot,"Heatmap", 1200, 1000)))
          }
        }else{
          cat(text_spec(
            "Heatmap skipped: fewer than two proteins remained after filtering invalid heatmap values.",
            italic = TRUE,
            font_size = "12px"
          ))
        }
        
        # Convert heatmap intensity columns to numeric
        significant_proteins_intensities[, 3:ncol(significant_proteins_intensities)] <-
          lapply(significant_proteins_intensities[, 3:ncol(significant_proteins_intensities)], as.numeric)
        
        # Create z-scored heatmap matrix
        significant_proteins_intensities_z <- cbind(
          significant_proteins_intensities[, 1:2],
          t(as.data.frame(scale(t(significant_proteins_intensities[, 3:ncol(significant_proteins_intensities)]))))
        )
        
        # Extract z-scored values
        z_heatmap_values <- significant_proteins_intensities_z[, -c(1, 2)]
        
        z_heatmap_values <- data.frame(
          lapply(z_heatmap_values, as.numeric),
          check.names = FALSE
        )
        
        # Filter rows that became NA/NaN/Inf after z-scoring
        keep_rows_z <- complete.cases(z_heatmap_values) &
          apply(z_heatmap_values, 1, function(x) all(is.finite(as.numeric(x))))
        
        significant_proteins_intensities_z <- significant_proteins_intensities_z[keep_rows_z, ]
        
        # Create matching mask for z-scored heatmap
        imputed_z <- imputed[keep_rows_z, ]
        
        if (nrow(significant_proteins_intensities_z) >= 2) {
          
          heatmap_plot_scored <- create_heatmap(
            significant_proteins_intensities_z,
            imputed_z,
            samples_names_comparison,
            group_ids_comparison,
            "Log Intensities Heatmap (Z-scored)"
          )
          
          if (format_svg) {
            cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(heatmap_plot_scored, "Heatmap_scored", 15, 15)))
          } else {
            cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(heatmap_plot_scored, "Heatmap_scored", 1200, 1000)))
          }
          
        } else {
          cat(text_spec(
            "Z-scored heatmap skipped: fewer than two proteins remained after filtering invalid z-scored values.",
            italic = TRUE,
            font_size = "12px"
          ))
        }
        
      # Add spacing after the heatmap section in the HTML report
      cat(text_spec("\n"))
      
  ########################## Summary table   ########################## 
      
      # Merge the raw mean intensities for significant proteins with the statistical results for the current comparison
      map = merge.data.frame(raw_intensities_significant_proteins,current_statDF,by=c("Id"))
      map$Accession <- map$Accession.x
      map$Label <- map$Label.x
      map <- map[, !(names(map) %in% c("Accession.x", "Accession.y", "Label.x", "Label.y")), drop = FALSE]
      map <- map[, c("Id", "Accession", "Label", setdiff(names(map), c("Id", "Accession", "Label"))), drop = FALSE]
      
      # Removing columns that are not needed in the displayed significant-proteins table
      significant_proteins_table <- map[, !(names(map) %in% c("mean_intensity", "significant")), drop = FALSE]
      
      # All remaining columns are assumed to be numeric result/intensity columns.  If not NA, use protein row in table
      for (i in 4:ncol(significant_proteins_table)) {
        significant_proteins_table[[i]] <- ifelse(
          is.na(significant_proteins_table[[i]]),
          NA,
          formatC(as.numeric(significant_proteins_table[[i]]), format = "e", digits = 5)
        )
      }
      
      # Creating HTML datatable and apply styling
      sig_dt <- DT::datatable(significant_proteins_table,
        rownames = FALSE,
        extensions = 'Buttons',
        options = list(
          dom = 'Bfrtip',
          buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel', 'pdf', 'print'),
          scrollX = TRUE
          )
        ) %>%
        DT::formatStyle(
          columns = colnames(significant_proteins_table),
          fontSize = '8pt',
          rowHeight = '30px'
        )
      
      print(htmltools::tagList(sig_dt))
      
    }
  }
  
  ########################## Add results to global table  ########################## 
  
  # Extracting the current comparison-specific statistical results from statDF (with anova / kruskall, the raw p-values of the
  # pairwise tests and the post-hoc p-values)
  current_statDF <- statDF[c("Id", "Accession", "Label", paste0("mean_intensity_", comparison), paste0("fc_", comparison), paste0("pval_", comparison),
                             intersect(paste0("posthoc_pval_", comparison), colnames(statDF)), paste0("qval_", comparison), paste0("significant_", comparison))]
  
  # Creating and filling log10 pvalue column
  current_statDF[[paste0("log10_pval_", comparison)]] <- -log10(current_statDF[[paste0("pval_", comparison)]])
  
  # Creating and filling qvalue column
  current_statDF[[paste0("log10_qval_", comparison)]] <- -log10(current_statDF[[paste0("qval_", comparison)]])
  
  # Creating and filling log2 fc column
  current_statDF[[paste0("log2_fc_", comparison)]] <- log2(current_statDF[[paste0("fc_", comparison)]])
  
  # Removed quotation marks from column names
  # colnames(current_statDF) = c("Id", "Accession", "Label", "mean_intensity", "fc", "pval", "qval", "significant")
  
  ########################## output tables   ########################## 
  
  # Create a comparison-specific name for teh label column
  new_name <- paste0("Label (", comparison, ")")

  # Adding imputed or unimputed data
  # (Accession and the log intensity columns of the A and B samples, in table order)
  log_suffix <- if (imputation) paste0(pattern, "_imputed_log") else "_mean_noimpute_log"
  to_add <- filtered_data[c(
    "Accession",
    intersect(names(filtered_data), group_cols(c(A_name, B_name), log_suffix, names(filtered_data)))
  )]
  
  
  # keep only columns not already in output_t, except Accession which is the key
  non_key_cols <- setdiff(names(to_add), "Accession")
  names(to_add)[names(to_add) %in% non_key_cols] <- paste0(non_key_cols, "_", comparison)
  to_add <- to_add[, c("Accession", setdiff(names(to_add), c("Accession", names(output_t)))), drop = FALSE]
  output_t <- merge(output_t, to_add, by = "Accession", all = TRUE)
  
  # Choose merge key
  if ("Id" %in% colnames(current_statDF) && "Id" %in% colnames(output_t)) {
    key_col <- "Id"
  } else if ("Accession" %in% colnames(current_statDF) && "Accession" %in% colnames(output_t)) {
    key_col <- "Accession"
  } else {
    stop("No common merge key found between current_statDF and output_t.")
  }
  
  # Select key plus columns not already in output_t
  stat_cols_to_add <- c(
    key_col,
    setdiff(names(current_statDF), c(key_col, names(output_t)))
  )
  
  # Keep only columns that really exist in current_statDF
  stat_cols_to_add <- intersect(stat_cols_to_add, names(current_statDF))
  
  stat_to_add <- current_statDF[, stat_cols_to_add, drop = FALSE]
  
  output_t <- merge(output_t, stat_to_add, by = key_col, all = TRUE)

  # A protein is kept for the statistical analysis of this comparison if it passed the comparison filter (it is in current_statDF).
  # For the first comparison, the "Label" column is the one of the input table (filled for every protein): it is emptied for the
  # proteins not kept, as the label columns of the other comparisons are.
  kept_in_comparison <- output_t[[key_col]] %in% current_statDF[[key_col]]
  output_t$Label[!kept_in_comparison] <- NA
  output_t$PresentInBoth <- kept_in_comparison


  # Get the column index of the column to be moved
  label_index <- which(colnames(output_t) == "Label")
  colnames(output_t)[label_index] <- new_name
  
  column_index <- which(colnames(output_t) == "PresentInBoth")
  colnames(output_t)[column_index] <- paste0("Kept for stat analysis (", comparison, ")")

  cdc <- grep(".*_log", colnames(output_t))
}

# Global test over all the conditions (anova or Kruskal-Wallis): p-values, and q-values with Test.adjust.procedure
# (with Test.type=anova or kruskall and more than one comparison)
if (export_global_test) {
  global_name <- if (Test.type == "anova") "anova" else "kruskal"
  global_table <- data.frame(Id = pvalue_table$Id, pvalue = as.numeric(pvalue_table$global_pval))
  colnames(global_table)[2] <- paste0(global_name, "_pvalue")
  if (Test.adjust.procedure != "none") {
    defined <- !is.na(global_table[[2]])
    global_q <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(global_table))
    if (any(defined)) {
      adj <- mt.rawp2adjp(global_table[[2]][defined], proc = Test.adjust.procedure, alpha = Stat.threshold.significance)
      global_q[defined] <- adj$adjp[order(adj$index), 2]
    }
    global_table[[paste0(global_name, "_qvalue")]] <- global_q
  }
  output_t <- merge(output_t, global_table, by = "Id", all.x = TRUE)
}

output_t <- rename(output_t, Accession_code = Accession)
output_t <- rename(output_t, GeneName = Gene_name)

indices <- match(og_Acc$Accession, output_t$Accession)
output_t <- output_t[indices, ]
```

```{r save_data}

############################################################
# Save DA output table
#
# Behavior:
# 1. If params$origin_file is a valid Excel workbook:
#      - load that workbook
#      - read its "Protein sets" sheet
#      - match by:
#            Protein sets$protein_set_id  <->  df/output_t$Id
#      - append quantification/statistical output columns into "Protein sets"
#      - remove "Parsed_proteins_set" if it exists
#
# 2. If no valid origin_file is available:
#      - create a new workbook
#      - write df + output_t side-by-side into "Parsed_proteins_set"
#
# In both cases:
#      - add/replace R_Params
#      - add/replace R_Metadata
#      - save DA_output_table.xlsx
############################################################


############################
# Helper functions
############################

replaceWorksheet <- function(wb, sheet_name) {
  
  if (sheet_name %in% names(wb)) {
    openxlsx::removeWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
  }
  
  openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
}


appendMatchedColumns <- function(base_df,
                                 add_df,
                                 base_id_col,
                                 add_id_col,
                                 columns_to_skip = character()) {
  
  # Match IDs as character to avoid numeric/character mismatches.
  base_ids <- as.character(base_df[[base_id_col]])
  add_df[[add_id_col]] <- as.character(add_df[[add_id_col]])
  
  # Avoid duplicated IDs in the table being added.
  # This prevents duplicated/ambiguous matches.
  add_df <- add_df[!duplicated(add_df[[add_id_col]]), , drop = FALSE]
  
  match_idx <- match(base_ids, add_df[[add_id_col]])
  
  # Columns to add, excluding the matching ID column and any explicitly skipped columns.
  cols_to_add <- setdiff(colnames(add_df), c(add_id_col, columns_to_skip))
  
  # Store final Excel/dataframe positions of newly added columns.
  added_positions <- integer(0)
  
  for (col_name in cols_to_add) {
    
    # If the column already exists in Protein sets, do not duplicate it.
    if (col_name %in% colnames(base_df)) {
      next
    }
    
    base_df[[col_name]] <- add_df[[col_name]][match_idx]
    added_positions[col_name] <- ncol(base_df)
  }
  
  list(
    data = base_df,
    added_positions = added_positions
  )
}


############################
# Prepare input paths
############################

source_file <- params$quant_df
source_ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(source_file))

origin_file_value <- ""

if (!is.null(params$origin_file)) {
  origin_file_value <- trimws(as.character(params$origin_file)[1])
}

use_origin_file <- (
  !is.na(origin_file_value) &&
    origin_file_value != "" &&
    tolower(origin_file_value) != "na" &&
    file.exists(origin_file_value) &&
    tolower(tools::file_ext(origin_file_value)) %in% c("xlsx", "xlsm")
)

############################
# Read quantification file
############################

if (source_ext %in% c("txt", "tsv")) {
  
  df <- read.delim(
    source_file,
    sep = "\t",
    header = TRUE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
} else {
  
  stop("Unsupported file type: ", source_file)
  
}

if (!"Id" %in% colnames(df)) {
  stop("The quantification file does not contain an 'Id' column.")
}

if (!"Id" %in% colnames(output_t)) {
  stop("output_t does not contain an 'Id' column.")
}


############################
# Create or load workbook
############################

if (use_origin_file) {
  
  output_file <- openxlsx::loadWorkbook(origin_file_value)
  
} else {
  
  output_file <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  
}


############################################################
# Main output sheet
############################################################

if (use_origin_file) {
  
############################################################
# Case 1:
# Merge df + output_t into the existing Protein sets sheet
############################################################

if (!"Protein sets" %in% names(output_file)) {
  stop("origin_file was provided, but the workbook has no 'Protein sets' worksheet.")
}

protein_sets <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(
  origin_file_value,
  sheet = "Protein sets",
  check.names = FALSE
)

if (!"protein_set_id" %in% colnames(protein_sets)) {
  stop("The 'Protein sets' worksheet has no 'protein_set_id' column.")
}

original_cols <- colnames(protein_sets)

############################################################
# Columns to skip because they are already represented in
# the original Protein sets sheet
############################################################

# In the intermediate quantification file, these duplicate information
# already present in Protein sets.
df_cols_to_skip <- intersect(
  c("Accession", "Gene_name"),
  colnames(df)
)

# In output_t, these are renamed versions of the same information.
# Also skip Description/Coverage if they accidentally exist in output_t
# from an older annotation block.
output_t_cols_to_skip <- unique(c(
  intersect(c("Accession_code", "GeneName"), colnames(output_t)),
  grep(
    "description|coverage",
    colnames(output_t),
    ignore.case = TRUE,
    value = TRUE
  )
))

############################################################
# Add quantification-file columns to Protein sets
############################################################

# Match:
# protein_sets$protein_set_id <-> df$Id

df_for_merge <- df
output_t_for_merge <- output_t
df_for_merge$Quant_file_Id <- df_for_merge$Id
output_t_for_merge$DA_output_Id <- output_t_for_merge$Id

# We skip Accession and Gene_name because Protein sets already contains
# equivalent annotation columns.
df_append_result <- appendMatchedColumns(
  base_df = protein_sets,
  add_df = df_for_merge,
  base_id_col = "protein_set_id",
  add_id_col = "Id",
  columns_to_skip = df_cols_to_skip
)

protein_sets <- df_append_result$data


############################################################
# Add DA output columns to Protein sets
############################################################

# Match:
# protein_sets$protein_set_id <-> output_t$Id
#
# We skip Accession_code and GeneName because they duplicate information
# already present in Protein sets.
output_t_append_result <- appendMatchedColumns(
  base_df = protein_sets,
  add_df = output_t_for_merge,
  base_id_col = "protein_set_id",
  add_id_col = "Id",
  columns_to_skip = output_t_cols_to_skip
)

protein_sets <- output_t_append_result$data
output_t_added_positions <- output_t_append_result$added_positions


############################################################
# Replace Protein sets worksheet with merged version
############################################################

replaceWorksheet(output_file, "Protein sets")

openxlsx::writeData(
  output_file,
  "Protein sets",
  protein_sets,
  startCol = 1,
  startRow = 1
)

worksheet_name <- "Protein sets"
existing_rows <- nrow(protein_sets) + 1

# Remove Parsed_proteins_set if it exists, because the requested output
# should only have Protein sets in the origin-file case.
if ("Parsed_proteins_set" %in% names(output_file)) {
  openxlsx::removeWorksheet(output_file, "Parsed_proteins_set")
}

# Set general column widths.
openxlsx::setColWidths(
  output_file,
  worksheet_name,
  cols = 1:ncol(protein_sets),
  widths = 10
)
  
} else {
  
  ############################################################
  # Case 2:
  # No origin_file, so create Parsed_proteins_set as before
  ############################################################
  
  # The parsed quantification columns are the original columns, the DA output columns are appended after them
  original_cols <- colnames(df)

  worksheet_name <- "Parsed_proteins_set"
  
  replaceWorksheet(output_file, worksheet_name)
  
  # Write the parsed quantification dataframe first.
  openxlsx::writeData(
    output_file,
    worksheet_name,
    df,
    startCol = 1,
    startRow = 1
  )
  
  existing_cols <- ncol(df)
  existing_rows <- max(nrow(df), nrow(output_t)) + 1
  
  openxlsx::setColWidths(
    output_file,
    worksheet_name,
    cols = 1:existing_cols,
    widths = 10
  )
  
  # Append output_t after df.
  openxlsx::writeData(
    output_file,
    worksheet_name,
    output_t,
    startCol = existing_cols + 1,
    startRow = 1
  )
}

###################################################
# Style header row of main output worksheet       #
###################################################

# Read the main output worksheet to determine how many columns it has.
main_sheet <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(
  output_file,
  sheet = worksheet_name,
  check.names = FALSE
)

main_sheet_cols <- ncol(main_sheet)

# Number of original columns before new merged data starts.
# This should be defined earlier in the script before adding/merging new columns.
# Example:
# original_cols <- colnames(protein_sets)
# n_original_cols <- length(original_cols)

n_original_cols <- length(original_cols)

# Original column headers: light green
original_header_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(
  fgFill = "#ccffcc",      # light green background
  fontColour = "#000000",  # black text
  textDecoration = "bold",
  halign = "center",
  valign = "center"
)

# New merged-data headers: light blue
merged_header_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(
  fgFill = "#cce5ff",      # light blue background
  fontColour = "#000000",  # black text
  textDecoration = "bold",
  halign = "center",
  valign = "center"
)

# Apply light green to the original columns
# (seq_len() and not 1:n, which gives c(1, 0) when n = 0 and creates an invalid cell in column 0)
if (n_original_cols > 0) {
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    output_file,
    worksheet_name,
    style = original_header_style,
    rows = 1,
    cols = seq_len(n_original_cols),
    gridExpand = TRUE,
    stack = TRUE
  )
}

# Apply light blue to the newly added / merged columns
if (n_original_cols < main_sheet_cols) {
  openxlsx::addStyle(
    output_file,
    worksheet_name,
    style = merged_header_style,
    rows = 1,
    cols = (n_original_cols + 1):main_sheet_cols,
    gridExpand = TRUE,
    stack = TRUE
  )
}

openxlsx::setRowHeights(
  output_file,
  worksheet_name,
  rows = 1,
  heights = 20
)

###################################################
# Conditional formatting for heatmap-like columns #
###################################################

# cdc contains column indexes relative to output_t.
# We handle the column positions differently depending on whether
# output_t was appended after df or merged into Protein sets.

if (exists("cdc") && length(cdc) > 0) {
  
  if (use_origin_file) {
    
    # In the origin-file case, output_t columns were merged into Protein sets.
    # Therefore, find the final Excel positions using output_t_added_positions.
    cdc_col_names <- colnames(output_t)[as.integer(cdc)]
    cdc_excel <- output_t_added_positions[cdc_col_names]
    cdc_excel <- as.integer(cdc_excel[!is.na(cdc_excel)])
    
  } else {
    
    # In the no-origin case, output_t starts immediately after df.
    cdc_excel <- as.integer(cdc) + ncol(df)
    
  }
  
  if (length(cdc_excel) > 0) {
    
    cdc_excel <- sort(unique(cdc_excel))
    
    indice_list <- c(
      0,
      which(unlist(diff(cdc_excel)) > 1),
      length(cdc_excel)
    )
    
    hm_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(numFmt = "0.00")
    
    rows_to_format <- 2:existing_rows
    
    for (index in 1:(length(indice_list) - 1)) {
      
      cols_to_format <- (
        cdc_excel[indice_list[index] + 1]
      ):(
        cdc_excel[indice_list[index + 1]]
      )
      
      openxlsx::conditionalFormatting(
        output_file,
        worksheet_name,
        cols = cols_to_format,
        rows = rows_to_format,
        type = "colourScale",
        style = c("green", "yellow", "red")
      )
      
      openxlsx::addStyle(
        output_file,
        worksheet_name,
        hm_style,
        cols = cols_to_format,
        rows = rows_to_format,
        gridExpand = TRUE
      )
      
      openxlsx::setColWidths(
        output_file,
        worksheet_name,
        cols = cols_to_format,
        widths = 4
      )
    }
    
  } else {
    
    cat("No cdc columns were added to the output sheet. Skipping conditional formatting.\n")
    
  }
  
} else {
  
  cat("No cdc columns found. Skipping conditional formatting.\n")
  
}


############################
# Save R parameters sheet
############################

replaceWorksheet(output_file, "R_Params")

openxlsx::writeData(
  output_file,
  "R_Params",
  parameters,
  rowNames = TRUE
)

params_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(fgFill = "lightyellow")

openxlsx::addStyle(
  output_file,
  "R_Params",
  params_style,
  cols = 1:2,
  rows = 1:(nrow(parameters) + 1),
  gridExpand = TRUE
)

openxlsx::setColWidths(output_file, "R_Params", cols = 1, widths = 30)
openxlsx::setColWidths(output_file, "R_Params", cols = 2, widths = 90)


############################
# Save experimental design sheet
############################

replaceWorksheet(output_file, "Exp_Design")

openxlsx::writeData(
  output_file,
  "Exp_Design",
  expDesign,
  rowNames = FALSE
)

openxlsx::addStyle(
  output_file,
  "Exp_Design",
  params_style,
  cols = 1:ncol(expDesign),
  rows = 1:(nrow(expDesign) + 1),
  gridExpand = TRUE
)

openxlsx::setColWidths(output_file, "Exp_Design", cols = 1:ncol(expDesign), widths = "auto")


############################
# Save metadata sheet
############################

replaceWorksheet(output_file, "R_Metadata")

openxlsx::writeData(
  output_file,
  "R_Metadata",
  analysis_metadata,
  colNames = FALSE
)

metadata_style <- openxlsx::createStyle(fgFill = "lightblue")

openxlsx::addStyle(
  output_file,
  "R_Metadata",
  metadata_style,
  cols = 1:2,
  rows = 1:nrow(analysis_metadata),
  gridExpand = TRUE
)

openxlsx::setColWidths(output_file, "R_Metadata", cols = 1, widths = 30)
openxlsx::setColWidths(output_file, "R_Metadata", cols = 2, widths = 200)


############################
# Save final workbook
############################

exit_address <- paste0(
  as.character(params$output_dir),
  "/DA_output_table.xlsx"
)

openxlsx::saveWorkbook(
  wb = output_file,
  file = as.character(exit_address),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```
